15.115: He studied the Vedas duly and virtuously and was established in penance. As good luck would have it, that knower of Dharma became inclined towards renunciation.
15.116: Eager that he was in the Self study (of the Vedas) and the performance of penance he resorted to holy centres.
15.117: There he saw a holy forest named Dhamnavana which affords the achievement of Dharma—a place accessible to the Yogins and inaccessible to the haters of Brahman.
15.118: A very holy and pure river named Mandakini flowed there. It was endowed with clusterous growth of red and blue lotuses and was bedecked with the hermitages of the Siddhas.
15.119: On its southern bank, he saw a beautiful and very holy hermitage occupied by leading sages and Yogins and felt delighted.
15.120: He propitiated Girisa (god Siva) by means of (reciting) Rudradhyaya and the CanVa (narrative) of Rudra, as well as by many different kinds of hymns of Sambhu, taken from the Vedas.
15.121: In the meantime (while praying) he saw the great sage named Svetasvatara coming. He was the most excellent among the great devotees of Pasupati (god Siva).
15.122: He had applied Bhasma (ashes) all over his limbs. The loin cloth was the only covering garment he had. His body was emaciated due to the performance of penance. He was wearing a white sacred thread.
15.123: After concluding his eulogy of Sambhu, he bowed down his head at his feet. His eyes were rendered dim due to tears (ofjoy). With palms joined in reverence, he spoke these words.
15.124: "I am contented, blessed. Since the leading sage and Yogin, the holy Lord, the most excellent among the knowers of Yoga has been personally seen by me.
15.125: Ah! My good luck is indeed great. My penances have become fruitful. What shall I do? O sinless one, I am your disciple. Save me."
15.126: He blessed the King of very good conduct and ■gentle behaviour. He accepted him as his disciple, for he had ■wiped off all his sins, thanks to his penance.
15.127: The clever sage made him perform all rites pertaining to sannjdsa and then bestowed on him the divine knowledge (about Siva) for which the holy rites had been laid down in his own branch of the Vedas.
15.128: He gave him the entire essence of the Vedas, that secures the release of the Pasu (Individual soul) from the Pdia (the binding noose of Avidyd). It is famous as the Antydiramd}- (the last stage of life). It has been performed by Brahma and others.
15.129: Glancing at all his disciples, those who resided in that hermitage viz. Brahmanas, Ksattriyas and Vaisyas who were all interested in maintaining celibacy, he said thus:
15.130: "It is only after studying the branch of knowledge initiated by me that the Yogins attain Mahadeva after medi¬ tating on the universe as the creation of the Lord.
15.131: It is here that the Lord Mahadeva sporting along with his consort Uma, occupies the place, with a desire to bless the devotees.
15.132: Formerly, Narayana himself, the creator of the entire universe, propitiated Mahadeva here with a desire for the welfare of the worlds.
15.133: It is after propitiating Lord Isana (Siva) the deity of even Devas, that Devas and Danavas attained great mira¬ culous powers here.
15.134: It was here itself that Marici and all other sages perceived Mahesvara through the power of their penance and attained eternal perfect knowledge.
15.135: Hence, O leading king, you too stay here practis¬ ing penance and Yoga. You stay with me permanently and thereby you will attain Siddhi."
15.136: After addressing thus, the leading Brahmana meditat¬ ed on Lord Siva, the wielder of the Pinaka bow. He then imparted precisely the great Mantra for the achievement of every thing ( v.l. of his objectives).
15.137: That Mantra suppresses all sins. It is the essence of the Vedas. It yields liberation. It is the holy Mantra begin¬ ning with the word Agni. It has been initiated (made to function) by the sages.
15.138: At his instance King Susila, endowed with faith, became a devotee of Pasupati and was engaged in the study of the Vedas.
15.139: He applied the sacred ashes (Aorma) all over his body. He lived on roots, fruits and bulbous roots. He was quie¬ scent and had full self-control. He subdued his anger and resorted to the procedure of renunciation.
15.140: Havirdhana begot a son named Pracinabarhis in Agneyi. He was a master of the science of archery.
15.141: Lord Pracinabarhis, who was the most excellent among the wielders of all sorts of weapons, begot of the daughter of the ocean, ten sons.
15.142: They were well known as Pracetasas. They were kings of reputed power. Devoted to Narayana, they studied their respective Vedas.
15.143: Daksa who had been the blessed son of Brahma formerly and a progenitor as well, was reborn of Marisa and the ten Pracetas collectively.
15.144: That Daksa carried on a verbal dispute with the intelligent Rudra, the great Isa. He was cursed by Rudra and he thereby became the son of Pracetas.
15.145: Seeing that Daksa was coming to his residence, he along with his consort personally accorded him befitting worship.
15.146: Then the son of Brahma (Daksa) who had been infested with the Tamo-Guna yearned for more worship than he deserved. He became infuriated and went away to his house (in a huff).
15.147: Once, when Sati had come to her own house, the evil-minded Daksa used word of abuse to her and angrily scolded her along with her husband.
15.148: ''All my other sons-in-law are superior to your hus¬ band the wielder of the Pinaka bow. You too are an evil daughter among my good daughters. Hence go away from this house (back to your place) in the manner you had come.
15.149: On hearing his words, the goddess, the beloved of Sankara censured her father, Daksa, and burned herself by means of her own self (by Yogic process).
15.150: After bowing to her husband Pasupati, the wearer of elephant's hide, she became the daughter of Himavan, being delighted at his penance.
15.151: On knowing her (dead in this manner) Lord Rudra, Kara, the dispeller of dejectedness of those who resort to him, became infuriated and after coming to his house, cursed Daksa.
15.152: 'After abandoning this body, born of Brahma, be born in the family of Ksattriyas. You will be a foolish-minded person and will beget a son of your own daughter.'
15.153: Imprecating him thus, Mahadeva went to the moun¬ tain Kailasa. Daksa too, the son of the self-bom deity (Brahma) became Pracetasa (son of the Pracetasas) in due course.
15.154: Thus all details of creation of Svayambhuva Manu, upto Daksa have been narrated to you. This story dispels the sins of those who hear this."
15.155: This protest against non-inclusion of god Siva'in the invitees of the sacrifice by sage Dadhica is not in the Bh. P. or NP. (both Vaisnava Puranas) but is found in the Vdyu 1.30.103-106 (but Dadhica's curse to all sages is not intheVayu), in SK. P. MaheSvara Kkapda 1.2.14-32 (but no curse by Dadhica but a simple walk-out), in SP. Rudra Samhitd 27.26-50 too, Dadhica protests and walks away. Dadhica's curse to all the sacrificial priests appears to be KP's contribution. KP, however, shares some verses with the Vayu e.g.
15.156: In the Bh. P. and other Puranas, Siva, as a revenge of the self- immolation of his consort Sati, destroyed the sacrifice of Daksa. In KP., however, the goddess (the daughter of Himavan) remembers her i-.sult in the previous birth by Daksa, when in his previous birth, he was her father, and in order to wreak revenge of her insult in that birth by her then father, she urges god Siva to destroy his sacrifice in this new incarnation!
15.157: I shall recount the creation of the subjects in con¬ tinuity with the previous kalpa as mentioned by Narayana. The story dispels sins and it will be sustained in all the three units of Time (i.e. the past, present and future).
15.158: On being cursed by Sambhu, Daksa, the Royal son of Pracetas, censured Bhava due to the previous enmity and performed a Tdjna (sacrifice) at Gangadvara (i.e. near the source of the river Ganga).
15.159: All Devas were invoked along with Visnu in order to receive their respective shares. All leading sages came there along with all other sages.
15.160: On seeing the entire host of Devas arrived, except¬ ing Sankara, the Brahmana sage named Dadhica spoke thus to Pracetasa (Daksa).
15.161: "How is it that Rudra is not being worshipped now duly—Rudra, the lord, whose behests every one beginning with Brahma and ending with the Pisacas (Ghosts), carries out?"
15.162: "In all Tajhas the share to Sankara is not allotted. Sankara is not being worshipped because there are no Mantras of Sankara along with his wife."
15.163: The infuriated great sage laughed at Daksa derisively and said these words even as all Devas were listening. The sage possessed all types of knowledge himself. He was as if an embodiment of knowledge).
15.164: "How is it that Sankara is not known well and hence not worshipped by means of all Tajnas? It is he who is known as Parameivara and it is from him, the soul of the universe that every thing begins to function, {v.l. He is the source of every thing).
15.165: "Indeed he is not Sankara (benefactor), but is Rudra, the annihilator. He is only the Tamasa (possessor of Tamo-gam) Hara. He is known as a naked mendicant holding the human skull. It is not proper to call him the soul of the universe.
15.166: Indeed Isvara, the lord and creator of the universe is Lord Narayana, Hari. This glorions Lord of Sattvic nature is worshipped in all holy rites."
15.167: "Is not this lord of a thousand rays (the sun-god) seen by you? He is the sole annihilator of worlds. He is Paramesvara in the form of Kala.
15.168: It is him that the righteous scholars, the expounders of the Brahman, pray to. He is the witness of everything. He is the body of Sankara of intense brilliance and he is of the form of Kala.
15.169: He is Rudra, the great god. He is the kind-hearted Hara, Kapalin {v. 1. of matted hair). He is the lord Aditya, the sun-god. He is the blue-necked and Vilohita (very ruddy).
15.170: He is eulogised as one of a thousand rays by the singers of Saman hymns, the Hotrs and the Adhvaryus. See him. ols Rudramurti (one of the terrible form), of the creator of the universe and an embodiment of three Vedas."
15.171: "The twelve Adityas have come here as the sharers in the Tajha. All of them should be known as suns. There is no other Sun."
15.172: When he said thus, the sages who had come to assist him as well as to witness the rajna said to Daksa, "That is exactly so."
15.173: Vasava (Indra) and all other Devas came there for their shares. They did not see Lord Isana (Siva) except Nara- yana, Hari.
15.174: Even as all of them were watching. Lord Hiranya- garbha (born out of a golden egg) Brahma, the most excellent among the knowers of Brahman vanished, in a moment.
15.175: When lord Brahma vanished, Daksa personally sought refuge in Narayana, Hari, the saviour of the worlds.
15.176: Then the fearless Daksa resumed the Tajna. Lord Visnu, the protector of those who seek refuge, was his patron deity (the saviour).

16.1: Observing that all Devas and sages were antagonistic to Rudra, the holy sage Dadhica spoke thus to Daksa:
16.2: "There is no doubt in this that a man incurs great sin in worshipping one who is not worthy of worship and in not worshipping those who deserve worship.
16.3: The terrible punishment meted out by divine interces¬ sion is sudden and terrible in that place where bad men are received well and good men are slighted."
16.4: After saying thus, the Brahmana sage cursed those Brahmanas who were antagonistic to Isvara (Siva) and who had come there to render assistance to Daksa.
16.5: After saying thus, the Brahmana sage, the storehouse of penance ceased (to speak). He mentally thought of Rudra, the destroyer of all sins.
16.6: In the meantime, the all-knowing goddess learnt this and spoke to the great god, Mahesvara, her husband as the lord of Pasus.
16.7: O Sankara, Daksa who had been my father in the previous birth is performing a Tajna after censuring your status and your own self
16.8: The gods and the great sages are assembled there rendering him assistance. Please destroy that sacrifice immediaely. I am choosing this boon.
16.9: Thus implored by the goddess, the great Lord, the Lord of Devas, created Rudra immediately with a desire to destroy the Yajha of Daksa.
16.10: Siva spoke to him thus: "O Ganesvara (leader of the attendants). Blessings unto you. After censuring me, Daksa is performing a Tajna, at Gahgadvara, (near the source of the river Gahga). Destroy that sacrifice of Daksa."
16.11: Then the sacrifice of Daksa was destroyed by Vira¬ bhadra playfully like a single lion released from bondage.
16.12: Bhadrakali, Mahesvari was created angrily by Uma. Gana (the attendant Virabhadra) rode on the bull and went along with her.
16.13: Thousands of other Rudras, who became famous as Romajas (born of hair) were created by that intelligent being in order to assist him (Virabhadra).
16.14: They wielded tridents, Saktis and iron clubs in their hands. They had sticks, pebbles and stones in their hands. They resembled Rudra and the Kalagni (terrible fire of dissolu¬ tion of the universe). They made the ten quarters reverberate with their shouts and sounds.
16.15: All of them were very terrible. Accompanied by their wives, they rode on the bulls. They went thus towards the place of sacrifice of Daksa, surrounded the leading Gana (i.e. Virabhadra).
16.16: "All of us are the followers of Sarva (Siva) of immeasurable brilliance. We have come here desirous of receiv¬ ing our shares. Give the desired shares to us.*
16.17: O excellent sages, if this is some one's deception,** let this be told that the shares are to be given to you and not to us."
16.18: Inform him, who commands you thus. We shall know from him. Devas the foremost among whom was Prajapati Daksa on being addressed thus, by the leader of Ganas, spoke:
16.19: It is him that the learned persons who have become merged in Brahman and who expound Vedas realise. He is the Atman of all living beings. He is the seed (cause) and the ultimate goal.
16.20: Thus, the entire story of destruction of Daksa's sacrifice has been recounted to you. Now listen to the progeny of the daughters of Daksa."
16.21: According to Vamana P. Gh. 63, the demon Andhaka was Siva's son entrusted as a foster-child to Hiranyaksa. Andhaka entertained erotic passion for his mother Parvati and demanded her of Siva. In response to Siva's challenge, he fought with Siva who discomfiting him transformed him into his Gaa chief called Bhrngi.
16.22: According to the Bh. P. VII.10.23, Nrsimha commanded Prahrada to occupy the throne of his father. VP.1.23.32 endorses the same. But here Prahrada crowned his uncle Hiranyaksa as the Daitya chief.
16.23: A thousand sons he begot of Asikni,' the righteous daughter of Prajapati Virana.
16.24: When those sons were lost through the deception of Narada, Prajapati Daksa, begot sixty daughters of Virini.®
16.25: You are all-pervading. All immortal Devas cons¬ titute your physical body. You are the eternal great Yogin. You are the Atman of all living beings. You are the Chief and great Prakrti.
16.26: You are interested and engaged in detachment and prosperity. You are beyond the scope of speech. You are pure. You are the maker and the sustainer. You are the annihilator of the enemies of gods.
16.27: ''This is that lord Narayana, the protector of Devas and our immutable enemy, or definitely his son."
16.28: After saying this, they showered a volley of arrows and other weapons on that Male being. That lord sportively destroyed them (the weapons). He was not wounded.
16.29: Because he was eagerly attached to the kingdom he was deluded due to the force of the curse. He began to harass the leading Brahmanas. He did not understand Visnu.
16.30: Due to the greatness of the previous impressions and culture, he regained his perfect knowledge of Visnu the great Purusa. He sought shelter in him, as he was worthy of being the refuge.
16.31: Thereafter, the leading Daitya had undeflected devotion to Visnu the most excellent of all Purufas and attained Yoga.
16.32: When the son of Hiranyakasipu became eagerly attached to Yoga, the leading Asura, Andhaka obtained (i.e. succeeded to) that kingdom.
16.33: (The Raksasa) the son of Hiranyaksa born of Siva's body, loved goddess Uma, the daughter of the mountain, stationed on Mandara.
16.34: Formerly, thousands of householder saints performed penance in order to propitiate Isvara, in the holy forest of Daruvana (Pine forest).
16.35: Then, once upon a time, a great drought insurmount¬ able due to its being of a long duration befell that country. It was very fierce and destructive of all living beings.
16.36: The sages who were overwhelmed with hunger, approached in a body to Gautama the storehouse of penance, and requested him for food for the sustenance of their lives.
16.37: That sensible sage gave them ample sweet cooked food of various kind. The Brahmanas partook of the food with their minds free from hesitatiori.
16.38: When the twelfth year elapsed as if the end of the world was over (and new order prevailed) bringing happiness and welfare to the world, the whole of the universe became as it was before (regained its previous stage).
16.39: Then all those leading sages took leave of one another. They said to the great sage Gautama—"We are going quickly."
16.40: He prevented them by saying thus, "O Scholars 1 Be pleased to stay comfortably at your pleasure in my house for some more time and you may go at your leisure."
16.41: Then all of them created an illusory black cow and took it near the noble-souled Gautama.
16.42: On observing it, the sage was overwhelmed with
16.43: Extremely distressed with grief, the great sage could not understand what should be done and what should not be done. The other sages spoke to that sage.
16.44: O excellent Brahmana, as long as the sin of the slaughter of the cow sticks to your person, food served by you should not be eaten. We are, therefore, going away.
16.45: On being permitted by him, they, being subject to this sin, went to the auspicious Devadaru Vana (Pine forest) in order perform penance as before.
16.46: By some reason the sage Gautama came to know of their fraud of imputing the sin of killing the illusory cow and cursed them in great anger.
16.47: "They will be ineligible for the study of the three Vedas and be on a par with the great sinners. As a result of this curse, they will be born again and again."
16.48: Then, glancing a t Visnu who was staying by his side, the bull-bannered lord said—"What is to be done in regard to those people who desire to acquire merit?".
16.49: After looking at the leading Brahmanas who had bowed down, lord Visnu, Hari, favourably disposed towards his devotees and worthy of being the refuge, spoke to Gopati (Lord of the Bull i.e. Siva).
16.50: "O Sankara! Not even particle of merit can go with (i.e. will be found in) a person excluded from the Vedas. For Dharma comes shining out of the Vedas.
16.51: Still, O Mahesvara, all these people, though they head on to hells, should be saved by us, in view of our affection towards our devotees.

17.1: Hence, O Bull-bannered lord, we shall compose scriptures for deluding the sinners and for saving those who are out of the pale of the Vedas."
17.2: Thus addressed by Visnu, the slayer of Mura, Rudra composed, deluding Scriptures and Kesava too did the same, on being urged by Siva.
17.3: They were the treatises of the cults of Kapala, Nakula, Varna, Bhairava, both of Western and Eastern variety, Pancaratra, Pasupata and thousands of other cults as well.
17.4: Only this Soul of the universe (Lord Siva), goddess Bhavani and Visnu know the Supreme Reality. I am verily desireless, quiescent, absolute and devoid of possession.
17.5: They call me Kesava and goddess Ambika as Laksmi. He is the creator and the dispenser of destiny. He is the cause as well as the effect.
17.6: Visnu does himself and makes others do. He is the bestower of worldly pleasures and liberation as the fruits (of actions). He is the enjoyer and the incomprehensible and unmeasurable Purusa. He is the annihilator, assuming the form of Kala.
17.7: He is the creator, protector, the pervading God, the soul of the universe, with faces in all directions. He is the indwelling soul of all, the immutable, all-pervader Yogin, Narayana, the undecaying Being.
17.8: Lord Visnu by his side and accompanied by the Chief leaders of Ganas, the son of Silada (i.e. Nandisvara) and the mothers, Lord Isa, Kala-Rudra went to fight.
17.9: * Seeing that the king of the chiefs of Ganas sur¬ rounded by the Lords of Ganas, had arrived, the enemy of gods (Andhaka) fought with god Indra, the 'mothers' and with the whole of army of Ganas as well as prominent immortals.
17.10: After defeating all by means of the prowess of his arms in the battle, he (i.e. Andhaka), riding his own aerial car, came to the place where Siva of infinite splendour and Kalarudra
17.11: On seeing Andhaka approaching, the Garuda-ban- nered Lord spoke to Bhairava, the great Lord besmeared with ashes as adornment.
17.12: "O Lord, it behoves you to slay Andhaka the lord of Daityas and a thorn unto the worlds. Excepting you there is no one else who can kill him.
17.13: You are the annihilator of all worlds, the lordly person, the embodiment of Kala. You are being eulogised by means of various Mantras by those persons who know the Vedas."
17.14: On hearing the words of Vasudeva, Lord Siva looked meaningfully at Visnu and determined in his mind to kill the lord of Daityas.

18.1: He went to the army of Devas which increased the delight of the Ganas. All beings moving about in the firmament eulogised lord Bhairava thus.
18.2: "Bevictorious O infinite Mahadeva, the embodiment of the eternal Kala. You are fire. You are omnipresent. You stay within all living beings.
18.3: You are the annihilator as well as the maker of the worlds (v.l. you are the sacrifice and the Va$at-kard ). You are the creator. You are the unchanging Visnu, god Brahma and Mahadeva. You are the Supreme lustre and the greatest abode.
18.4: You are OmAara incarnate, the Soul of Yoga, with three Vedas as your three eyes. You are the Lord of the universe endowed with Supreme potency. Be victorious, O infinite master of the world."
18.5: Thereafter, this controller of the world Kalagni- rudra, the goal of the good, pierced Andhaka with the tips of his trident and danced.
18.6: On seeing Andhaka transfixed to the trident, god Brahma and the groups of Devas bowed to Lord Bhairava, the releaser from worldly bondage.
18.7: The sages and siddhas eulogised him. The Gandharvas and Kinnaras sang. The charming groups of celes¬ tial damsels danced in the sky.
18.8: Fixed to the tip of the trident, the demon Andhaka had all his sins burned down. He gained perfect knowledge of
18.9: "I bow down my head to the only lord with great concentration. I bow down to the ancient holy one whom they know as the Principle of Isa. He is the Kala of infinite form. He is the poet, the cause of Toga (union) and Viyoga (separa¬ tion).
18.10: I bow unto you the absolute Rudra, who are terrible due to the curved fangs, who dance in the firmament, giving out fire from your mouth, whose form is that of the blazing sun and who are endowed with a thousand feet, eyes and heads.
18.11: Victory to you, the primordial deity whose feet are worshipped by the immortals. You are indivisible, a personifica¬ tion of the pure spirit. You are the one (sacrificial) fire worship¬ ped in various ways; you abide in all souls through external differences.
18.12: They call you the only ancient Purusa, with the brilliance of the sun and beyond darkness. You observe all this and protect it eternally. You are the annihilator, who are served by the groups of Yogins.
18.13: You are the only inner soul and conscience placed in many ways in the different bodies, but you are devoid of peculiarities of the bodies, etc.
18.14: You are the imperishable Brahman, the most sacred form, embodiment of bliss called Pranava (Om). You are the wellknown Self-born Isvara, ths master of those who know Vedas, devoid of all special characteristics.
18.15: You are of the form of Indra, Varuna and Agni. You are haihsa (swan), prana (the vital breath), death and final destruction. You are Yajna, Lord Prajapati. You are eulogised as the unique blue-necked god, by those who know the Vedas.
18.16: You are Narayana, the beginningless cause of the world. You are Pitamaha (grandfather) and Prapitamaha (great-grandfather) [of the universe]. You are sung about in the occult passages of Vedanta and the mystic Upanisads. You are the ever-auspicious (Sadasiva), Supreme Ruler (Paramesvara).
18.17: Obeisance to the greatest Being beyond darkness (of ignorance), the great Atman pervading the fourteen worlds. Salute to one who has excelled the three Saktis, to the unsullied one stationed in the seat of thousand Saktis (poten¬ cies).
18.18: Obeisance to the triple-formed deity whose personal form comprises infinite region, who is the receptacle of the world and its embodiment. Salute to you who are stationed in. the heart of the people. Bow to you the wearer of the great serpent as a necklace.
18.19: O lord, whose lotus-like feet are worshipped by the leading sages and siddhas! Obeisance to one who is firmly seated in the seat of prosperity and piety; Obeisance to the ultimate end, to the source of origin of the worldly existence, the embodiment of a thousand moons and a thousand suns.
18.20: Obeisance to one who is accompanied by Uma, of beautiful waist. Golden-armed Lord, obeisance to you. Salute to one with the fire, the moon and the sun as eyes. Bow to the gracious consort of Ambika.

19.1: Obeisance to the mysterious Lord concealed within the inmost cavity of the heart. Salute to the Lord who can be properly comprehended by the perfect knowledge of Vedanta. Bow to the great God Siva who is (transcendental to and there¬ fore) devoid of the three times (past, present and future), whose abode (or lustre) is o f spotless splendour.
19.2: Thus eulogised, the glorious lord set him down from the tip of his trident. Being pleased with him, he touched him with both of his hands and spoke thus:—
19.3: "O Daitya, in every respect I am pleased with this eulogy now. After attaining the status of the leader of Ganas, stay forever in my vicinity.
19.4: You shall be free from ailments. All your doubts will be cleared. You will be worshipped well, even by Devas. Be the follower of Nandisvara; be devoid of all miseries".
19.5: On seeing him thus, they were surprised much; they eulogised the Daitya. Lord Visnu smilingly said to the lord of Devas.
19.6: "O Mahadeva, your greatness is but meet and proper. A really great man does not take cognizance of defects due to one's caste ( v.l. ignorance). He takes in account their good attributes.
19.7: On being addressed thus, Bhairava, the leading Deva and Chief of the Ganas, went near Sankara accompanied by Kesava and the Daitya Andhaka.
19.8: Isvara (Sankara) grasped the son of Hiranyaksa (Andhaka) with his hand and went to the place where there stood the aerial chariot of the daughter of the mountain. On seeing her husband, the remover of worldly distress arrived along with Andhaka, the beloved of Isa expressed happiness and pleasure on behalf of Andhaka.
19.9: When Andhaka saw Mahesvari at the side of the lord, he fell on the ground like a staff; he bowed down at the lotus-like feet of the goddess—"I bow down to the beloved of the lord, the beginningless one, the daughter of the mountain from whom Pradhana and Purusa originate and who destroys the entire universe.
19.10: I bow unto that daughter of Himalaya mountain, who is unchanging and who shines in the purest golden seat of Siva along with him, within whom the entire universe is held and wherein all the worlds undergo dissolution. I bow down to that Uma who is devoid of all defects, (v.l. One who is adored by god as well as by demons).
19.11: She is not born, she does not become decreased, she does not increase. I bow down to that Uma who transcends all Gunas. I bow down to the daughter of the lord of mountains. O Goddess, O daughter of the mountain, forgive what has been committed by me out of delusion. I bow down to your lotus-like feet saluted by Devas and Asuras.
19.12: Thus eulogised by the lord of Daityas, humble with devotion, the blessed goddess Parvati accepted Andhaka as her son.
19.13: Then at the behest of Sambhu, the great lord Bhairava, born of Rudra, went to Patala along with the matriarchs.
19.14: It was here that the Tamasa form of Visnu, the cause of annihilation of the world existed. The unmanifest lord Hari remains there in the form of Nrsirhha (Man-lion).
19.15: Then Sambhu of the form of Ananta (the infinite) was well worshipped by even Sesa; Lord Kalagni Rudra united his own Atman to the Supreme Soul.
19.16: Even as the lord was in the Yogic unison, the hungry mothers bowed down to the three-eyed Mahadeva and said to him:
19.17: "O Mahadeva, we are hungry. It behoves you to permit us. We shall eat up the three worlds. We will have no satisfaction otherwise."
19.18: After saying this much, the Mothersborn of Visnu, devoured the three worlds including the mobile and immobile beings.
19.19: Then lord Bhairava meditated on lord Narayana, Hari with the physical form of Man-lion and bowed down to him with palms joined in reverence.
19.20: After reaching the vicinity of Visnu, all those des¬ tructive deities transferred their powers unto Sambhu, Bhairava, of excessive refulgence.
19.21: The mothers then saw the most terrible Man-lion, the source of origin of the universe, and the serpent Sesa attain¬ ing unity instantaneously.
19.22: "Those who are the devotees of the trident-wielding lord and those who remember me should be assiduously protected.
19.23: This unequalled form that destroys everything is my own, and is born of Mahesvara's person. It bestows worldly pleasures and liberation.
19.24: Lord Kala, the infinite and the four-faced Brahma, the god of gods are but two aspects viz. Tamasa and Rajasa, of mine, (the former being characterised by the Tamasa and the latter by the Rajasa aspect).
19.25: It is I that utterly unthwartable god Kala, the calculator of the universe, who, at the end of the kalpa, will devour the entire universe by assuming the form of Rudra.
19.26: That fascinating form of mine which abounds in Sattva gum and is called Narayana, stabilises and protects the universe for ever.
19.27: That Visnu, the greatest Brahman, the Supreme Atman, the ultimate goal, the unmanifest primordial nature, is mentioned as Sadananda (ever blissful)."
19.28: The goddesses, the Vaisnavite matriarchs who were thus enlightened by Visnu sought ultimate refuge in that great lord alone.
19.29: The episode of the incarnation of Mahavisnu as the son of Aditi- Kasyapa and his subsequent assumption of the cosmic form, etc. as given here closely follows the version in the Bh. P. VIII skandha & not the one in Pd. P. wherein he (Mahavisnu) pushes the demon Dhundhu the same way. The significant difference between the Vamana episode in the KP & Bh. P. is that in the KP. Sukra does not come in the way of Bali while he was about to donate three paces of land, and Visnu does not push Bali down to the nether world. Bali saw the transformation of the dwarf Vamana into the cosmic figure and occupying the three worlds with three steps and his re¬ assumption of a dwarf (Vamana) form. He completes the formality of gift by pouring water on his hand and as p)er his advice enters Patala to lead a life devoted to Visnu.
19.30: The KP. differs from the NP. about the end of Virocana. Here he is said to have abdicated the throne in favour of his son Bali and have resorted to the path of Yoga, while in the NP he, at the request of his queen, gave up his life as a price for the water used for washing the feet of the old Brahmin (god Visnu in disguise).
19.31: While he was reigning thus, once, the holy lord, the great sage, Sanatkumara came to his city at the instance of Visnu.
19.32: The great Asura who had been seated on the throne, got up and went near the son of Brahma. He bent down his head and with palms joined in reverence, spoke these words.
19.33: "Blessed I am and favoured with grace, since the glorious Lord of Yogins, the expert knower of the Vedas or Brahman, has today personally visited my excellent town.
19.34: O scholarly Brahmana, why have you come? You are the lord Pitamaha himself. O son of Brahma, tell me, what behest shall I carry out for you?
19.35: The holy lord spoke to the great Asura endowed with piety: I have come here to see you. You are very fortunate.
19.36: O excellent Daitya, this sort of policy is very rare among Daityas. There is certainly no other righteous person like you in the three worlds.
19.37: The king of Asuras who had been addressed thus, spoke again to the great sage—O holy one, the most excel¬ lent among the knowers of Brahman, elucidate unto me the greatest of all virtues.
19.38: The glorious Yogi imparted to the noble-sou led king of Daityas the secret-most perfect knowledge of the Atman which is the highest Dharma.
19.39: Having obtained the greatest knowledge and given Dakfina (money by way of fees) unto the preceptor, he entrusted the burden of kingdom to his son and he became interested in the regular practice of Yoga.
19.40: That son of his was the great and intelligent Asura named Bali. He was favourably disposed towards Brahmanas. He was extremely virtuous. Then he conquered Purandara.
19.41: Indra, surrounded by all Devas fought a great battle with him. On being defeated, he sought refuge in lord Visnu, Acyuta (the infallible).
19.42: In the filament of the lotus of her heart, she con¬ centrated her mind on Vasudeva, the unsullied great region, devoid of beginning and end, the blissful, unique firmament.
19.43: The delighted lord Visnu, Hari the wielder of a conch, a discus and a mace {Sankha, Cakra and Gada), the Yogic Atman appeared in front of the mother of Devas.
19.44: On seeing Visnu arrived, Aditi endowed with devotion considered herself as having attained her objects. She propitiated Kesava with the following eulogy.
19.45: Be victorious, O sole cause of destruction of all (lit. the floods of) miseries; Hail to you. Hail to you, O Lord, endowed with the advent of infinite greatness, glory to you. O Lord, with perfect knowledge as your physical form, O Lord devoid of beginning, middle and end. Victory to you, O one resembling the Ether; O one with unsullied bliss as your form
19.46: Obeisance to Visnu of the from of Kala. Salutations to you the Man-lion. Bow to you, to Sesa, Obeisance to Kalarudra, the cause of annihilation; Obeisance to you Vasudeva, salutations to you.
19.47: Obeisance to you, the wielder of Universal Maya. Obeisance to you, the Reality, comprehensible only through Yoga. Obeisance to you, founded in virtue and perfect knowledge. Obeisance to you, Varaha (the divine Boar); Obeisance to you again and again.
19.48: Obeisance to you, O Lord with form resembling (re¬ fulgent like) a thousand suns and moons. Obeisance to you, O Lord, accessible only through perfect Vedic knowledge and piety. Obeisance to the upholder of the Earth. Obeisance to the unmeasurable. Obeisance to you, O Lord, the source of the origin of the Universe. Obeisance again and again unto you.
19.49: Obeisance to you, Sambhu founded in truth. Salu¬ tations to you, the cause of and embodiment for the form of the universe. Obeisance to you stationed in the middle of Yogic seat (meditation). Obeisance to you, the auspicious one of single form. Salutations to you again and again.
19.50: Lord Visnu, identical with the universe, who was thus propitiated by the mother of Devas, laughingly told her to choose the boon she wished.
19.51: Bowing down her head on the ground, she chose the excellent boon—"For the welfare of Devas, I choose this boon that pray, you be my son."
19.52: The Lord favourably disposed towards those who resort to him said, "So be it." The incomprehensible Lord vanished there itself, after granting the boon.
19.53: After a lapse of time the mother of Devas conceived Janardana, Lord Narayana himself, in her womb.
19.54: When Hrsikesa occupied the womb of the mother of Devas, evil portents of terrible nature happened in the city of Bali, the son of Virocana.
19.55: On seeing the evil portents, the leader of the Daityas became agitated due to fear. He bowed to Prahlada, the aged Asura and his grandfather, and said to him:—
19.56: "O grandfather of great intelligence, why does this portentous phenomena happen in this city of ours. What may be the reason thereof? What should be done now"?

20.1: After hearing his words, and meditating for a long time, the great Asura bowed down to Hrsikesa and spoke these words;
20.2: "For the purpose of slaying the Asuras, the mother of the heaven-dwellers has conceived in her womb that Visnu who is v/orshipped by means of Tajhas and to whom belongs this entire universe.
20.3: That Vasudeva from whom everything is non-differ- ent and who differs from everything, has entered the womb of the mother of Devas.
20.4: That Lord Visnu whose form even Devas do not know precisely, has entered today the body of Aditi by his own wish.
20.5: That Hari, the ancient Purusa, the great Yogin from whom the living beings originate, and wherein they attain dissolution, has now incarnated.
20.6: That Visnu, wherein the conception of name, caste, etc. has no place and who is of the mere form of existence, is being born with a portion of himself.
20.7: That Janardana, whose power is the mother of the Universe, Maya, goddess Laksmi, who is the sustainer of the Dharma, has incarnated.
20.8: He whose form constituted of Tamas is Rudra and whose body is formed of the Rajo-gma is Brahma and whose form sustained by Sattva-guna is Visnu.
20.9: Thinking thus about Govinda, with a mind humble due to devotion, seek shelter in him alone. Thereby, you will attain great bliss."
20.10: Thereafter, at the instance of Prahlada, Bali, the son
20.11: When the proper time arrived, Aditi, the mother of Devas, bore to Kasyapa, the son, Mahavisnu himself, the increaser of the delight of Devas.
20.12: (She gave birth to Vi?nu) who had four arms and large eyes, whose chest is marked by Srivatsa emblem, who resembles the blue cloud (in complexion), who was resplendent and surrounded by glorious halo (Sri—or goddess of wealth).
20.13: Devas, Siddhas, Sadhyas, Garanas, of whom Indra was the head and Brahma surrounded by the groups of sages approached Upendra* (god Visnu) (for worshipping him).
20.14: Lord Hari, whose investiture with the sacred thread was performed, studied the Vedas and the code of good con¬ duct from Sage Bharadvaja holding it as a model for the people in the three worlds.
20.15: Thus the Lord points out the worldly course of con¬ duct. The common people follow what he does as they consider him the authority.
20.16: Then, in course of time, the intelligent Bali, son of Virocana, worshipped Visnu, the all-pervading Lord of Yajnas by performance of Yajnas.
20.17: He worshipped Brahmanas after giving them abun¬ dant wealth. Brahmana sages came to the sacrificial hall of the noble soul.
20.18: Lord Vi?nu came to know of this and urged by Bharadvaja, he came to the place of Yajna assuming the form of a Vamana (Dwarf).
20.19: With the hide of a black antelope and the sacred thread (as the upper garment) and shining with the sacred staff of a Palasa tree in his hand, the extremely brilliant Brahmana (Visnu, the Dwarf) with matted hair, came there reciting the Vedas.
20.20: Coming near the king of Asuras, Hari the mendicant begged him for the space traversed by three steps of his own feet.
20.21: The Lord of the Daityas had sought refuge in him. Desirous of making him free from covetousness and other passions, the primordial Lord covered, in his strides, the Earth, firmament and heaven.
20.22: The foot of the Lord traversed the three worlds, and went to the Brahmaloka from the region of Prajapati. The leading gods, the chief of whom were the Adityas, and the Siddhas who stayed there bowed unto him [v.l. who was refulgent like a thousand suns.]
20.23: The Primordial Lord, the beginningless grandsire of the world, offered worship to him and propitiated him. After cracking the Upper crest of the Cosmic egg, he em¬ bellished with divine ornaments went again.
20.24: Thanks to the breaking of the Egg, the great cool water resorted to by the meritorious, flowed over. The excellent river was designated as Ganga by god Brahma. It was stationed in the sky.
20.25: After reaching the great Prakrti, Pradhana, the source of Brahman and then the sole Purusa, the seed (origin) of the universe, he stabilised his foot at the unchanging region of I sa. Seeing it, the gods eulogised it at those different places.
20.26: On seeing that Purusa with the universe for his physical body, Bali the great, bowed to Visnu with devotion.
20.27: Lord Vasudeva, the primordial creator became a Dwarf once again and said to him—"O Lord of Daityas, in effect, the three worlds have been given over to me by you yourself."
20.28: Bowing down again his head, the Daitya poured water at the tip of his hand (and said), "I shall offer myself unto you of infinite splendour and abode, to Trivikrama of unmeasured stride."
20.29: After accepting dana (lit. what has been offered) from Bali, the son of Prahlada's son, Sahkha-pani (i.e. the conch¬ armed deity Visnu), the immanent soul of the universe spoke again to Daitya: "Enter the root (the downmost part) of the nether world.
20.30: Enjoying pleasures unavailable even to gods, stay there permanently. By the path of devotion, meditate on me continuously. At the close of the Kalpa, you will enter me once again."
20.31: After advising this to that lion-like Daitya, Visnu of great strides and of truthful exploits, gave the three worlds unto Indra.
20.32: Siddhas, Devas, sages, Kinnaras, gods Brahma, Indra, Lord Rudra and Adityas (the sun-gods) and the group of Maruts eulogised the Deity of great Yoga.

20.39: That king was a great devotee of Sankara. He ruled over the kingdom. After subjugating the three worlds, he harassed Indra.

21.1: O Brahmanas, Surasa gave birth to a thousand serpents as well as to thousands of noble-souled, multi-headed, heaven-wanderers.
21.2: Arista gave birth to a thousand Gandharvas. Ananta and other great serpents are glorified as the sons of Kadru.
21.3: O leading Brahmanas, Tamra gave birth to six daughters Suki, Syeni, Bhasi, Sugriva, Granthika (v.l. Grdh- rika) and Suci.
21.4: Surabhi gave birth to the cows and buffaloes. Ira gave birth to trees, creepers, vines and grasses of all kinds.
21.5: Similarly, Muni gave birth to Yaksas, Raksasas, and Apsaras. O excellent saints, it was out of anger that she gave birth to the groups of Raksasas.
21.6: The two famous sons of Vinata were Garuda and Aruna. Out of them, intelligent Garuda performed a very difficult penance. Thanks to the favour of the Trident-bearing deity, he attained the status of the vehicle of Hari.
21.7: Aruna propitiated Lord Mahadeva by means of penance. He was engaged in the charioteer-hood of the Sun- god by Sambhu who was pleased with him.
21.8: These mobile and immobile beings are the des¬ cendants of Kasyapa born in the Vaivasvata Manvantara which have been described to you. It destroys the sins of those who hear.
21.9: O man of holy vows, the twenty-seven daughters of Daksa are said to be the wives of the Moon. There were many (v.l. sixteen) children born to the wives of Aristanemi.
21.10: Svastyatreya is the seer of two sOktas of the RV—V. 50, 51. It is; reasonable to assume that he was the son of Atri and Svastyatreyas are his descendants.
21.11: Suka is a celibate recluse in the Bh. P. The Devi Bhagavata (Skandha I) credits him with a wife, Pivari, daughter of Pitrs and four sons—Krsna, Gauraprabha, Bhuri, Devasruta and a daughter, Kirti who was given in marriage to Anu, the son of King Vibhraja. The information in KP. about the sons and daughters of Suka is different though both agree that Suka raised a family.
21.12: From Vatsara were born Naidhruva and Raibhya of very great fame. The sons born of Raibhya were Sudras (?) (v.l. Vaidyas) ♦ who were the most excellent among the learned ones (or knowers of Veda).
21.13: The daughter of Gyavana named Sumedhawas the wife of the noble-souled Naidhruva. She gave birth to the sons called Kundapayins.
21.14: A son called Devala who was devoted to the Brahman (or expert in the Vedas) was born of Asita and Ekaparna. He was a preceptor of Yoga and performed great penance.
21.15: Sandilyawas extremely glorious, pure and a knower of the true principles. By the grace of the Lord of Parvati, he attained the Yogic liberation (v.l. attained excellent Yoga).
21.16: O Brahmanas, the three sons, viz. Sandilya, Naidhruva and Raibhya of the family of Kasyapa had human tempera¬ ment (or are the sources or patriarchs of human beings). I shall now mention the children of Pulastya.
21.17: O Brahmanas, the daughter of Trnabindu was named Ailavila. The royal sage gave that daughter in marriage to sage Pulastya.
21.18: The son of Ailavila was the sage Visravas. He had four wives who made the family of Pulastya flourish.
21.19: They were Puspotkata, Vaka, Kaikasi and Deva- varnini. Listen to the progeny of these who were richly en¬ dowed with comely features and beauty.
21.20: The children begot of Vaka were Mahodara, Pra- hasta, Mahaparsva, Khara and the daughter Kumbhinasi.
21.21: Trisiras, Dusana and Vidyujjihva of great strength were also his sons. Thus there were these ten Raksasas of cruel actions in the family of Pulastya. All of them were endowed with the power of penance and physical strength. They were the devotees of Rudra and were extremely terrible.
21.22: Pulaha's sons were the deer, serpent, fanged beasts, Bhutas (goblins), PiMcas, bears, boars and elephants.
21.23: In the Vaivasvata Manvantara, Kratu was childless. Kasyapa who himself was a Prajapati, was the son of Marici.
21.24: Sukra the preceptor of the Daityas and a sage of great penance was born of Bhrgu. He was engaged in selfstudy of Vedas and the practice of Yoga. He was a devotee of Hara and was excessively brilliant.
21.25: Atri's son was Vahni and his uterine-brother was Naidhruva. It is heard by us that sons were born of GhrtacI from Krsasva, the Brahmana sage.
21.26: He begot of her Svastyatreyas' of great prowess. They were devoted to Vedas and Vedahgas and had destroyed thei r sins through penance.
21.27: Narada gave the gentle lady Arundhatl to Vasistha. As a result of the curse of Daksa, Narada led a celibate life.
21.28: When Haryasvas (the sons of Daksa) were lost due to the Maya (delusive advice) of Narada, Daksa with eyes red shot with anger cursed Narada.
21.29: "O Brahmana, since all my sons were destroyed by you through deceitfulness, you will be devoid of issues."
21.30: Vasistha begot of Arundhatl the son Sakti. From Sakti was born the glorious Parasara, the omniscient and the most excellent among the performers of penance.
21.31: After propitiating the Lord of the chief of Devas, Isana, the slayer of the Tripuras, he obtained the unrivalled son—the holy Lord Krsnadvaipayana.
21.32: §uka was born of Dvaipayana. It was Lord Sankara himself who incarnated on the Earth with a part of his personality and then attained his own great region. This Suka had five sons who were great ascetics. They were Bhurisravas, Prabhu, Sambhu, Krsna and Gaura, the fifth.
21.33: He had daughters ako viz. Kirtimatl, Yogamata and Dhrtavrata. These persons of the family of Atri, the expounders of Brahman, have been narrated by Brahma. Henceforth (listen to) and understand the royal progeny (born) from Kasyapa.
21.34: These verses emphasize the identity of the sun-god, Siva, Brahma as they are the forms of one Reality [ekath sat), the Para-brahman.

21.37: He was his eldest son. He had fifteen sons. The eldest of them was Kakutstha. Kakutstha's son was Suyodhana.
21.38: The glorious Prthu was born of Suyodhana. Visvaka was Prthu's son. From Visvaka was born the intelligent Ardraka, Yuvanasva was his son.
21.39: "After propitiating the primordial person Narayana, free from ailments, the Lord without beginning or destruction, one shall obtain a righteous son.
21.40: By propitiating the ruler of the Universe, the pri¬ mordial Kr?na whose son is Brahma himself and whose grandson is Nilalohita (i.e. Siva), one begets a good son.
21.41: By propitiating Hrsikesa, whose power and influence even Lord Brahma does not comprehend factually, one shall have a righteous son."

21.43: O excellent Brahmanas, it is said that Dhundhu¬ mara had three sons. They were Drdhasva, Dandasva and Kapilasva.
21.44: Pramoda was the son of Drdhasva, his son was Haryasva, Nikumbha was the son of Haryasva and from Nikumbha was born Sarhhatasva.
21.45: Krtasva and Ranasva were the sons of Sarhhitasva; Yuvanasva whose strength in battle was equal to that of Indra was the son of Ranasva.

22.7: On hearing these statements that saintly king be¬ came highly delighted in his mind. He bowed to and worshipped them. After bidding farewell to them, he spoke to Tridhanvan.
22.8: "By means of penance I shall propitiate the Lord designated with the single syllable OM, the great Purusa, the vital spirit stationed in the middle of Aditya.
22.9: But you should be devoted to Dharma forever. Eternally vigilant, protect the entire earthly realm consisting of the four castes of people."
22.10: After saying so, the sinless king entrusted the king¬ dom to the care of his son. In order to perform the excellent penance, he went to the forest.
22.11: Resorting to the forest of Devadaru {Pinus Devadaru) trees on the beautiful peaks of the Himalaya, he worshipped gods with bulbous and other roots and fmits grown in the forest and subsisted on them.
22.12: Shaking off his sins by means of penance, he mentally repeated the Mantra of goddess Savitri, the mother of the Vedas, for a hundred years and more.
22.13: While he was performing penance like this, the self- born lord, the great Isvara, Hiranyagarbha, the Atman of the Universe came to that spot himself
22.14: On seeing Lord Brahma with faces all round, coming there, the king bowed down his head at his feet and glorified his name.
22.15: "Obeisance to you O Brahman, the supreme God, the Supreme Soul, the gold-complexioned creator with a thousand eyes.
22.16: Salutations to the creator and the dispenser of destiny. Hail to you the embodiment of all gods. Obeisance to you, the embodiment of spiritual knowledge, comprehensible through the knowledge and practice of Sarhkhya and Yoga.
22.17: Obeisance to you, the Trinity, the Creator, the Omniscient One. Hail to the ancient Purusa, the preceptor of the Yogins."
22.18: Then, lord Brahma, the creator of the Universe, be¬ came delighted and said,—"Welfare unto you. Choose the boon. I am the granter of boons."

22.20: Glancing at the king, the Atman of the Universe (i.e. Brahma) said—"So be it". Stroking him gently with his hands, the delighted Lord vanished there itself.
22.21: The glorious king on securing the boon was much delighted, and he repeated the Japa. He was tranquil. He used to take his holy ablution thrice a day and he subsisted on fruits, roots and bulbous roots.
22.22: When hundred years were completed, the lord of fierce-rays (the Sun-god), the great Yogin, appeared in front of him from the middle of the Solar sphere.
22.23: On seeing the eternal Lord stationed in the solar sphere, the self-born lord Brahma, the embodiment of the Vedas, he was surprised.
22.24: With his mind overwhelmed with great emotion and with extremely deep devotion, he bowed down his head and eulogised him with the Savitri Mantra.
22.25: "Obeisance to you the blue-throated Lord, the brilliant Paramesthin. Salutations to Rudra of the form of the three Vedas {Trayi). Obeisance to the embodiment ofKala, the cause of all."

23.1: Hariscandra had a valorous son known as Rohita. Rohita's son was Vrka from whom was born Bahu.
23.2: Harita was Rohita's son. Dhundhu was his son.. Vijaya and Sudeva were the two sons of Dhundhu.
23.3: Vasistha of great splendour begot of the wife of Kalmasapada the son, Asmaka who became a noble scion of the Iksvaku dynasty.
23.4: From Raghu was born Aja and king Dasaratha was born of him. The heroic Rama, the world famous knower of Dharma, was the son of Dasaratha.
23.5: Bharata, Laksmana, and Satrughna of great strength also were his sons. All of them were equal to Indra on the battle-field. They were endowed with Visnu's Sakti.
23.6: Visnu, the enjoyer of the whole universe, was born with a part of his personality for the destruction of Ravana. The blessed wife of Rama was the beautiful daughter of Janaka.
23.7: After being crowned by Bharata, the powerful and highly splendoured Rama duly honoured the Brahmanas and worshipped Isvara.
23.8: He worshipped god Sankara the destroyer of Daksa's Tajna, by performing a horse-sacrifice. Rama begot a son who was well-known by the name Kusa.
23.9: Lava also, the highly fortunate and intelligent one knowing all principles and topics, was his son. Atithi was born of Kusa and Nisadha was his son.
23.10: Nala was the son of Nisadha. Nabhas was born of him. Pundarikaksa was born of Nabhas and Ksemadhanvan was his son.
23.11: His son was the heroic Devanika of great valour. Ahinagu was his son and had Mahasvan as his son.
23.12: From him was born Gandravaloka. Taradhisa was his son. Gandragiri was born of Taradhisa. Then was born Bhanuvitta.
23.13: Srutayu was born of him. These are the descendants born in the race of Iksvaku. O excellent Brahmanas the im¬ portant ones have been narrated in brief.
23.14: He who listens to this excellent race of Iksvaku everyday shall be freed from all sins. He is honoured in the heavenly region.

23.17: We have heard the report that five heroic sons of great prowess were born to Ayus from Prabha, the daughter of Svarbhanu.
23.18: Among those five, Yayati was the strongest and most valiant. He married DevayanI, the daughter of Usanas (Sukra).
23.19: He married Sarmistha also, the Asura lady, the daughter of Vrsaparvan. DevayanI gave birth to Yadu and Turvasu.
23.20: The king entrusted the South-western territory to the care of the eldest son Yadu. He appointed Druhyu and Anu tn rule over the western and northern territories respectively.
23.21: The whole of this Earth was righteously ruled by them. The king of great fame, thereafter, went to the forest accompanied by his wife.
23.22: Yadu too had five sons comparable to the sons of Devas. They were Sahasrajit, the most excellent Krostii, Nila, Jina and Raghu.
23.23: The son of Sahasrajit was the king Satajit. Satajit too had three highly virtuous sons.
23.24: They were Haihaya, Haya, and the King Venuhaya. Haihaya had a son who became well-known as Dharma.
23.25: O Brahmanas, his son was Dharmanetra the valor¬ ous. Dharmanetra's son was Kirti and Sanjita was his son.
23.26: Mahisma was the son of Sanjita whose descendant son was Bhadrasrenya. Bhadrasrenya's successor was the king called Durdama.
23.27: Durdama's son was the intelligent and valiant king named Andhaka. Andhaka's four successors were highly res¬ pected by the public.
23.28: He had hundreds of sons. But five of them were great heroes. They were well-versed in the use of miraculous missiles, heroic, strong, virtuous and learned.
23.29: They were Sura, Surasena, Krsna and Dhrsna, as well as Jayadhvaja, the powerful king who was devoted to Narayana.
23.30: The first four sons viz. Sura and others were well- known for their prowess. They were noble souls, devoted to Rudra, used to worship god Sankara.
23.31: Jayadhvaja was intelligent and devoted to religion. He sought shelter under Narayana, Visnu, Hari.
23.32: The other sons told him—"O sinless one, this is not your Dharma as it is well-known that our father was engaged in the propitiation of Isvara (Siva)."
23.33: The highly brilliant son (Jayadhvaja) replied to them: "This is my highest holy duty as all the kings in the world have been born through the parts of Visnu.
23.34: The protector of a kingdom is certainly the Lord Purusottama. The unconquered Visnu, Hari, the protector of the worlds, should be worshipped.
23.35: It has been proclaimed that the self-born deity has three forms—constituted of Sattva, Rajas and TomaJ respectively and they are the causes of creation, sustenance and destruction of the universe.
23.36: Lord Visnu, the Sattvic soul forever sustains (the universe). The Rajasaic form Brahma creates and the Tamasa form Rudra annihilates it.
23.37: Hence, Lord Visnu, Kesava the suppressor of Kesin, is the deity worthy of being propitiated by kings who protect their respective kingdoms."
23.38: On hearing his words, the other steady-minded bro¬ thers said,—"Rudra, the annihilator should be worshipped by those who seek liberation.
23.39: This Rudra is verily the Supreme Deity. At the end of the Kalpa period. Lord Siva, resorting to the Tamo-guna, will annihilate the whole of this world.
23.40: The trident-bearing lord dissolves the world by means of Vidya at the outset* and then by means of his Supremely terrible and the most refulgent form."
23.41: Then pondering over it, king Jayadhvaja spoke to- them—"The creature is liberated through Sattva Gum and Lord Hari is constituted of Sattva Guna."
23.42: The brothers replied to him—"If Rudra is served by the Sattvika people he liberates them. One who is endowed with Sattva Guna shall always worship Siva."
23.43: Then prince Jayadhvaja laughingly remarked:—"It is proper that one's own Dharma should be followed for salva¬ tion. No other method is prescribed by sages.
23.44: So the propitiation of Visnu of unmeasured prowess is the greatest Dharma of kings who always uphold the power derived from him."
23.45: Another son of the king, Kfsna the most excellent among the intelligent ones, spoke to him—"What our father Arjuna has done is the holy dharma.''
23.46: When the dispute thus continued Surasena spoke these words—"In this matter the sages are our authority. What they say in this matter must be correct."
23.47: Then all those prominent among kings being ex¬ tremely agitated in mind, went to the hermitage of Seven sages who were the expounders of the Brahman (or the Vedas) and usked them.
23.48: Those sages headed by Vasistha and others conveyed to them the truth in matter:—"Whatever deity appeals to a man is his deity.
23.49: But if the deity is worshipped for a specific purpose it bestows what is liked by men. By special worship it bestows everything. O kings, this principle or rule cannot be other¬ wise.
23.50: The deities of kings are:— Visnu as well as Isa (Siva) and Purandara (Indra). The deities of Brahmanas are:—Agni (the fire-god), Aditya (the sun-god), Brahma and the Pinaka-wielding deity (Siva).
23.51: The deity of Devas is Visnu, of Danavas is the Trident-bearing lord; Soma (moon) is said to be the deity of Gandharvas and Yaksas.
23.52: The deity of Vidyadharas is the goddess of speech; of Siddhasis Lord Hari; of Raksasas is Sankara, Rudra and of Kinnaras is Parvatl.
23.53: The deity of sages is, Lord Brahma as well as Mahadeva, the wielder of the trident. Goddess Uma is worthy of being respected by women, so also are Visnu, Isa and Bhas- kara (the sun-god).
23.54: All these are the deities of householders. The Brahman shall be the deity of Brahmacarins (religious students under the vow of celibacy). The deity of Vaikhdnasas (recluses) shall be Arka (the sun-god) and the deity of ascetics {Sannyasins) shall be Mahesvara.
23.55: The god of goblins is Lord Rudra, that of Kusrnandas is Vinayaka, and the deity of every one is Lord Brahma, the progenitor and the lord of devas.
23.56: Lord Brahma himself has proclaimed thus. Hence Jayadhvaja certainly deserves the propitiation of Visnu.
23.57: But Hari should be worshipped by men after realising his identity with Rudra. Otherwise Hari may not annihilate the enemy of the king."
23.58: Thereafter, they bowed to them and returned to their extremely splendid city. After conquering the enemies in the battle, they protected the Earth.
23.59: O Brahmanas, then, on one occasion  a certain Danava named Videha who terrified all beings, came to their city.
23.60: He was terrible due to his fangs; his body was blazing (i.e. he had a resplendent personality) like fire at the world-destruction, at the close of Tugas. He was wielding a spear sparkling like the sun. His roaring sound reverberated in the ten quarters.
23.61: Men who lived there lost their lives on hearing that shout; others became frightened and fled.
23.62: With great determination they rushed at Videha. Sura discharged the miraculous weapon of Rudra; Surasena hurled the missile of Varuna.

24.1: He is Visnu having the four manifestations [Vyuhas) but he himself is said to be devoid of Vyuha. He is the great Atman, the Supreme abode, the highest firmament. He is the ultimate highest region.
24.2: Expounders of Brahman call him the Brahman of three syllables OM. He is Vasudeva, the soul of the universe, the Yogic Atman and the Supreme person.
24.3: Devoid of passion, they worshipped the unchanging Rudra accessible through Tajna, through the performance of Yajna. The holy sage, venerable Vasistha, the knowerof Dharma, presided over their Tajna.
24.4: After realising Visnu as the greatest form of Rudra, Jayadhvaja performed the worship of Visnu assiduously.
24.5: He who always listens to this story of exploits of Jayadhvaja shall be freed from all sins. He goes to the region of Visnu.
24.7: This romantic dalliance between king Durjaya and heavenly damsel Urvasi seems to be the special contribution of the KP., as PE. is silent about it despite the seven Dur jayas mentioned on P. 255. The source of this legend is obviously the Vedic dialogue between Pururavas and Urvasi.
24.8: Vr?a was the founder of their family. His son was Madhu. Madhu had a hundred sons, but Vrsana only had continued his race.
24.9: Vitihotra's son was well-known as Ananta. Durjaya who was an expert in all sacred lores, was his son.
24.10: His wife was very beautiful and endowed with all good virtues. She was chaste, devoted to her husband, and she assiduously performed her religious duty, alongwith her husband.
24.11: Once, that great king saw the celestial damsel UrvasI seated on the banks of Yamuna singing in sweet tone.
24.12: With his mind struck by the cupid, he approached her and said:—"O celestial lady, it behoves you to indulge in sexual intercourse with me for a long time."
24.13: On seeing the king endowed with comely features and beauty like another god of love, the celestial lady indulged in amorous sports with him for a long time.
24.14: Becoming enlightened after a long time, the king said to the charming Urvasi—"I shall go to my beautiful city." She then laughingly said these words:
24.15: "O charming king, I am not fully satisfied with this much of enjoyment with you. You must stay one more year."
24.16: The intelligent king told her, "I shall go to the city and shall come back immediately. It behoves you to permit me.
24.17: That beautiful lady spoke to him,—"My dear king I agree. But you must not indulge in sexual intercourse with any other celestial lady."
24.18: 'Amen' said he, and immediately went to his ex¬ cellent city. After returning there, he saw his chaste wife and became extremely frightened.
24.19: On seeing him alarmed, his chaste wife of good qualities, the lady with plump breasts, spoke to him with pleas¬ ing words.
24.20: "O Lord, why are you under the spell of fear. Such fear is not conducive to the enhancement of your reputa¬ tion as a king."
24.21: On hearing her words, the king was overwhelmed with shame in his mind. He did not speak anything. But she knew everything through her vision of knowledge.
24.22: "O king, you need not be afraid. Atonement must be made by you for your sin. O great king, if you are afraid, your kingdom will go to ruins."
24.23: On the way, the leading king saw in the sky, a very excellent Gandharva bedecked in a divine garland, shining gloriously.
24.24: O Brahmanas, the invincible king defeated him in the battle and seized the garland. Eager to see that celestial damsel, he went to Yamuna.
24.25: Unable to see her there and afflicted by the arrows of the god of love, Kama, he wandered all over the Earth con¬ sisting of seven continents.
24.26: It is heard that in his eagerness to see UrvaH, he crossed the ridges of the Himalayas and scaled Hemakuta, the most excellent mountain.
24.27: In all these difiFerent places, excellent celestial ladies saw him, the king of brave exploits, bedecked in the wonder¬ ful garland. They were smitten with violent love for him.
24.28: Remembering the warning (lit. words) of UrvasI and with his mind exclusively attached to her, he did not care to glance at any of them at all, and he climbed the peaks of the mountain.
24.29: Not seeing the celestial damsel there also, he became all the more afflicted by passion. Endowed with divine exploits, he went to the great Meru, the region of Devas.
24.30: Facilitated by the strength of his arms, he crossed over the peak and reached the lake Manasa well known in the three worlds.
24.31: He saw the lady of spotless limbs on its banks. The blessed lady was playfully moving about there and he gave her the garland.
24.32: On seeing her bedecked in the garland, he was much fascinated.Realising that he was the most blessed, he had sexual dalliance with her for a long time.
24.33: At the end of the sexual intercourse, UrvasI enquir¬ ed of the leading king,—"O heroic king, what was done by you after going to the city?"
24.34: He told her everything that had been advised to by his wife, his meeting with Kanva and the seizing of the garland.
24.35: On hearing what had been mentioned by him, the celestial lady, his well-wisher, spoke to him—"Go. Otherwise Kanva will curse you and your beloved wife will curse me."
24.36: Though entreated by her thus repeatedly, the great king was so much fascinated by her charms and was so comp¬ letely attached to her in his mind, that he refused to comply with her request.
24.37: Then UrvasI who could assume any form as she pleased, always exhibited to the king her hideous form, which was very ugly, full of hair and with tawny coloured eyes.
24.38: For twelve years, he restricted his diet to fruits, roots and bulbous roots. Then the king spent another twelve years subsisting on the air only.
24.39: He went to Kanva's hermitage and out of fear, told him everything, his cohabitation with the celestial lady and his performance of excellent penance, once again.
24.40: On seeing that tiger-like (great) king, the holy sage became delighted. Desirous of eradicating even the seeds of his sins, he advised thus:
24.41: "Go to Varanasi, the divine city inhabited bylsvara. Lord Mahesvara resides there in order to liberate the whole- world.
24.42: By taking holy ablution in Gahga, by propiti¬ ating the deities and Pitrs duly and by seeing the Lihga of Visvesvara, you will be liberated from sins instantaneously."
24.43: He bowed down to Kanva with his head, and received his permission. The invincible king had the vision of Hara at Varanasi and became absolved of all sins.
24.44: He went back to his splendid city and performed a sacrifice on the Earth. On being requested, the sage Kanva, out of compassion, presided over the sacrifice.
24.45: His son was the intelligent Supratika. People acclaim¬ ed him as their king since his very birth.
24.46: From Urvasi, he had seven sons, comparable to- Devas and endowed with great prowess. All of them took daughters of Gandharvas as their wives, O Brahmanas.
24.47: Thus, the excellent race of Sahasrajit has been re¬ counted to you. It is a race that dispels sins of men. Now hear and understand the dynasty of Krostu too."
24.48: This indicates the lower social status of the Satvata Sastra in its early stage.

24.51: From him was born Prthuklrti, whose son was Prthudana. His (Prthudana's) son was Prthusravas and his son was Prthusattama.2
24.52: Usanas was his son. His son was Satesu. From him was born Rukmakavaca whose son was Paravrtta.
24.53: Yamagha (Jyamagha) well known all over the world was born as his son. From him was born Vidarbha. Kratha and Kausika were born of Vidarbha.
24.54: Lomapada was his third son. King Babhru was his (Lomapada's) son. His* son was Dhrti whose son was Sveta.
24.55: The powerful son of Sveta is called by the name Visvasaha. His son Kausika of great virility is known for his prowess.
24.56: The chief among them was Dyutiman. His son was Vapusman. Brhanmedhas was Vapusman's son whose son was Srideva.
24.57: O Brahmanas, his son was Vitaratha. He was very powerful. He was a devotee of Rudra. Kratha's son was Kunti and Vr?ni was his son.
24.58: I pay obeisance to the three-eyed, moon-crested ■goddess born of Hiranyagarbha (god Brahma) who is the Supreme Bliss, the digit of Cit (the consciousness aspect of the Brahman, nay) the very embodiment of the Brahman itself.
24.59: He worshipped goddess Sarasvati by means of differ¬ ent Tajnas and Homos (sacrificial offerings). His son was Dasaratha who was extremely virtuous.
24.60: He was a devotee of the goddess Sarasvati and was endowed with great splendour. Sakuni was his son. From him was born Karambha. His son was Devarata.
24.61: He performed a horse-sacrifice. Devaksatra was his son. His successor was Madhu and from him was born Kuru.
24.62: He had two sons viz. Sutraman and Anu. Ann's son was Priyagotra. The inheritor of his riches was Aihsu.
24.63: Aihsu's son was a valorous devotee of Visnu, Andhaka (v.l. satvata"") byname. He was a noble soul, engaged in charitable gifts. He was the foremost among those who know Dhanurveda (the science of Archery).
24.64: At the instance of Narada, he, engaged in worship¬ ping Vasudeva, composed the sacred scripture (usually) listened to by Kunda (son born of an adulterous woman), Gola (widow's son) and others.
24.65: A great scripture well known after his name, auspi¬ cious to Satvatas and conducive to the welfare of Kunda and others has been still current.
24.66: Satvata was his son. He was expert in all scriptures (or branches of knowledge) and a great king of meritorious reputation. They say that sacred lore (viz. Satvata Sastra) was founded by him.
24.67: While performing penance he wished thus: May a son endowed with good qualities be born to me." A king of auspicious fame, and a sovereign ruler over all, well known as Babhru was his son.
