25.1: Nimi and Krkana were the most well-known and the most important among them. Bhojas and Vaimatrkas were born in the family of Mahabhoja.
25.2: From Vrsni were born Sumitra, the powerful, as well as Anamitra and Timi. From Anamitra was bom Nighna. Nighna had two sons.
25.3: They were the highly fortunate Prasena and the excellent one named Satrajit. From Anamitra, the son of Vrsni, was born Sini (rather 'Sini') as the youngest son.
25.4: He was truthful in speech. He was richly endowed with fidelity. Satyaka was his son. Satyaka's son was Yuyudhana. His son was Asahga.
25.5: He begot of her a virtuous son named Akrura. He had many other sons Upamahgu, Mahgu and others.
25.6: Akrura's son was well known as Devavan and the divine-souled Upadeva who had sons called Visva and Prama- thin.
25.7: Citraka's sons were Prthu, Viprthu, Asvagriva, Subahu, Sudhasvaka (v.l. Suparsvaka) and Gaveksaka (v.l. Gavesana).
25.8: He begot of the daughter of Andhaka, four sons, viz. Kukura, Bhajamana, Samika and Balagarvita.
25.9: Kukura's son was Vrsni and Vrsni's son was Kapotaroman and his son was Vilomaka.
25.10: The scholarly Tama (v.l. Nala) a friend of Tum- buru was his son. The son of Tama was Anakadundubhi.
25.11: He went to Govardhana and performed extensive penance. Lord Brahma, the supreme Ruler of the worlds, grant¬ ed a boon to him.
25.12: To him who was engaged in music. Lord Siva, the consort of Parvatl, gave the jewel of a girl inaccessible even to Devas.
25.13: Thereafter, the mother taught that beautiful son in his childhood as well as the daughter, the art of music systematically.
25.14: After the investiture with the sacred thread, he learned the Vedas from a preceptor. He married the mental daughter of the Gandharvas (or a Gandharva girl called Manasi).
25.15: In her he begot five excellent sons, who knew the technique of playing on the Vina and were experts in the science of music.
25.16: Accompanied by his sons, grandsons and wife, the king, a wise and expert musician, worshipped the lord (Siva), destroyer ofTripuras, by means of music.
25.17: A Gandharva named Subahu took Hrimati who was beautiful in all limbs, with large eyes like Sri, to his city.
25.18: To that Gandharva of good refulgence, these sons were born of her—viz. Susena, Dhira, Sugriva, Subhoja and Naravahana.
25.19: Abhijit was the son of Candanodakadundubhi* (?) Punarvasu was born of Abhijit. Ahuka was born thereafter.
25.20: O excellent Brahmanas, Ahuka had two sons, viz- Ugrasena and Devaka. Devaka's sons were born heroes com¬ parable to Devas.
25.21: They were Devavan, Upadeva, Sudeva and Devaraksita. They had seven sisters. He gave them to Vasudeva.
25.22: Subhumi, Rastrapala, Tustiman and Sanku (also were his sons). The well-known son Viduratha was born of Bhajamana.
25.23: His son was Surasama (equal to the Sun) and from him was born Pratiksatra. From him was born Svayambhoja. From him was born Dhatrika, the chastiser of his enemies.
25.24: Krtavarma was his son. Surasena was his son. Vasudeva was his son who was engaged in religious rites.
25.25: From Vasudeva was born the powerful-armed Vasu¬ deva, the preceptor of the universe. Hari (Visnu), on being requested by Devas, became the son of Devaki.
25.26: The blessed lady Rohini, the splendid wife of Vasu- deva, gave birth to Sahkarsana, the eldest son known as Rama, with a plough as his special weapon.
25.27: Vasudeva, pervading the universe was the supreme Atman himself. Lord Sarhkarsana, the wielder of the plough as his weapon was Sesa himself
25.28: Under the pretext of Bhrgu's curse, he honoured a human body. Madhava was born of DevakI as well as of Rohini.
25.29: Kausiki, the Yogic-slumber born of Uma's body, became the daughter of Yasoda, at the behest of Vasudeva.
25.30: O excellent sages, the sons born to Vasudeva as elder brothers of Vasudeva had been killed by Karhsa already before.
25.31: When Rama was born, Devaki gave birth to Krsna, Acyuta, the first among Devas, the Atman whose chest had been marked by the curl of golden hair called Srivatsa.
25.32: Rama's wifewas Revati by name. Shewas endowed with good qualities. He begot of her two sons Nisita and Ulmuka.
25.33: Srikrsna, of indefatigable activities had sixteen thousand wives. The sons born to them were hundreds and thousands.
25.34: On seeing the heroic sons born to Rukmini from Janardana, Jambavati, his wife of pure smiles, said to Krsna.
25.35: "O slayer of Danavas, O lotus-eyed one, please grant me a son of excellent qualities, who will be honoured by- lord of Devas."
25.36: On hearing the words of Jambavati, Jagannatha, Hari, himself a store of penance, the suppressor of enemies, began to perform a penance.
25.37: O excellent sages, listen how the son of Devaki per¬ formed a severe and great penance, saw Rudra and obtained a son.
25.38: Savarni of Somadatta clan was one of the six disciples of Roma- harsana. He is credited to have composed a Purana Samhita of his own vide VP. III. 6 16-18, Bh. P. XII. 7.5-7.
25.39: Though A.S. Gupta emends this verse as kapeyo samsapayanah Vayu II. 61.56-58 mentions 'Susarma of Saihsapayana Gotra' as the disciple of Romaharsana. He is said to have composed a Purana Sarhhita of 8600 verses vide my Intro, to the A'P p. 3.
25.40: The correct reading appears to be "Saihsapayana.'
25.41: (Defective) The Brahmana popularised the meritori¬ ous Purana-sarhhita by the favour of excellent Brahmanas (?). Here the Purana narration of Vaisampayana® was proclaimed by his disciples.
25.42: Yajhavalkya, ihe great Yogin, perceived Hara here by means of his penance and composed the excellent Yogasastra as directed by him.
25.43: 11 was here that Bhrgu performed an unprecedented great penance formerly and obtained from Mahesvara, the son Sukra who was the most excellent among the knowers of Yoga.
25.44: Hence O, lord of Devas, perform a very severe penance here itself. You really deserve to visualize the terrible fierce Kapardin, the lord of the universe."
25.45: After saying thus, the great sage Upamanyu granted the perfect knowledge, the holy rite pertaining to Pasupata doctrine and its yogic practice to Krsna of indefatigable activity.
25.46: Advised thus by the excellent sage. Lord Madhu- sudana (the slayer of Madhu) propitiated lord Rudra there itself, by means of penance.
25.47: He smeared Bhasma (ashes) all over his body. He tonsured his head and wore bark garments. With his mind exclusively dedicated to Siva, he performed Japa (muttering the mantra) of Rudra continuously.
25.48: Then after a lapse of a long period, the great god Mahesvara (Siva) accompanied by Uma and decorated with a half-moon on his crest was seen by him in the sky.
25.49: He saw Mahadeva alongwith the goddess. He had a crown, he wielded the iron club. He wore garlands of variegated colours. He held the Pinaka bow and the trident. The lord of Devas had covered all his limbs by means of a tiger-skin garment.
25.50: He saw in front of him Sambhu, the lord of the vital airs {Prams) —the lord, the ancient Purusa who is eternal and who is a Yogin and the overlord of infinite power who is minuter than the minutest.
25.51: He saw the three-eyed lord whose hand wielded an axe, whose body was smeared with ashes and who was covered with the hide of a man-lion; who was uttering the Pramva OM, who was huge in size and (in resplendence) who resembled a thousand suns.
25.52: He saw in front of him Rudra, the primordial deity whose prowess neither Devas nor god Brahma, the grandsire of the world, nor Indra, nor fire-god, nor Varuna, nor the god of Death could describe in full, even to this day.
25.53: Then he observed on the left of Girisa his self, the unmanifest form of infinite, who was eulogising the lord by means of many words of praise and who was the primordial deity whose hands held conch, sword and discus.
25.54: On his right side, he saw a Puru$a (Being) with palms folded in reverence and seated on a swan. He was the Lord of Devas, the grandsire of the Universe, the preceptor of the world, stationed in heaven. He was eulogizing the great prowess of Isa (God Siva).
25.55: He saw in front of the ruler of the three worlds the chieftains of the Ganas (attendants) resembling a thousand suns (in brilliance), Nandisvara and others of immeasurable prowess, Kumara, as refulgent as the fire and Ganesa as well.
25.56: In front of him, he saw sages Marici, Atri, Pulaha, Pulastya, Pracetas, Daksa, Kanva, Parasara, Vasistha and Svayambhuva Manu.
25.57: Then contemplating over the universal Atman within his self {Atman), the noble-minded Visnu, with his palms folded bowed down with devotion to god Siva alongwith his heavenly consort Parvati and eulogised the chief of all gods (viz. Siva) with sacred hymns.
25.58: "Obeisance be to you, O eternal one! O, posses¬ sor of all Yogas (v.l. source of the universe)! Brahma and other sages regard you as Tamas, Sattva, Rajas and the mixture of all these three. Saintly people call you alone as 'All' (identical with everything) (or embodiment of everything like sattva, rajas and tamas.
25.59: O Rudra, you are Brahma and Hari. You are the maker of the Universe and its annihilator. You reside in the orb of the sun. You are the Prana (vital breath), the fire-god, Indra and other different beings. I seek refuge in you alone, the God and the Lord.
25.60: The Sarhkhyas (the followers of the Saihkhya school ofPhilosophy) say that you are one (the invaritable form),devoid ofGunas. Those who abide by Yoga system of philosophy always worship you as enthroned in the heart. The Vedas mention you
25.61: By offering a single flower or leaf at your foot, one becomes released from the bondage of the world. By remem¬ bering the pair of your feet served by Siddhas and Yogins, one dispels all sins by means of your grace.
25.62: OM, Obeisance to the blue-throated, three-eyed (Siva, the velocity incarnate). Obeisance, again and again to you forever, O Mahadeva, Isana.
25.63: Obeisance to you the wielder of the Pinaka bow. Salutations to the staff-bearer of tonsured head. Bow to you, the wielder of thunderbolt in the hand, to god with matted hair {Kapardin) and with the quarters for your robes.
25.64: Obeisance to you of terrible roar, to the fanged one, the embodiment of Kala. Bow to one with the serpent for your sacred thread; salutation to you with fire for your semen.
25.65: Obeisance to you, Girisa, to you Svahakara (the consecrator by the utterance of Svahd). Salutations to you who laugh boisterously. Obeisance again and again to the terrible one.
25.66: Obeisance to you, the destroyer of Kama. Bow to the Suppressor of Kala. Salutation to Hara of terrible apparel, to Hara, the archer.
25.67: Obeisance to you the three-eyed, the elephant- hide-robed one; salutation to the lord of Parvati. Bow to the lord of Pasus (Individual souls).
25.68: Obeisance to you of the form of the firmament; obei¬ sance to the lord of the firmament; to the one with a body half female and half male; obeisance to the promulgator of Sarhkhya and Yoga systems of philosophy.
25.69: Bow to the ruler of Bhairavas. Obeisance to one whose Lihga is worshipped by Devas. Salutation to the father of Kumara. Obeisance to you, the lord of Devas.
25.70: Obeisance to the lord of Yajnas, the ideal celibate. Obeisance to the great hunter of deer. Salutation to the overlord of Brahma.
25.71: Obeisance to Hama (the Swan), to the universe; salutations again and again to the fascinating one. Obeisance to you, the Yogin, to one accessible through Yoga, the master of Yogic Maya.
25.72: Obeisance to you, the protector of life, to one fond of the sound of bells; obeisance to you, bearer of the skull; obei¬ sance to the lord of luminaries.
25.73: Obeisance, again and again be to you. Salutations, again and again, O Paramesvara, grant unto me all of my desires."
25.74: O Brahmanas, after eulogising the lord of Devas thus with devotion, (Krsna) Madhava fell at the feet of the lord and the goddess (Uma) prostrate like a staff.
25.75: After lifting up Kr?na, the slayer of Kesin, the lord accompanied by Uma spoke these sweet words with the majestic- rumbling sound of a cloud.
25.76: "O Lotus-eyed Krsna, why is this penance being performed by you? You alone are the bestower of all desires and holy rites.
25.77: Indeed you alone are that great form of mine named Narayana. O Purusottama, the entire universe, cannot exist without you.
25.78: O Narayana, you know the infinite Atman, the Supreme Lord, Mahadeva, the master of great Yoga, by means of your own Yoga, O Kesava."
25.79: On hearing his words, Krsna laughingly gazed at the bull-bannered lord of the universe, and the goddess, the daughter of the mountain Himavan and addressed:
25.80: "O Sankara, everything has been understood by you by means of your own Yoga. O bestower of bliss, I wish to have a son equal to me. Grant unto me a son who will be your devotee."
25.81: "So be it" said the Atman of the universe, Kara with a delighted mind. Looking at the goddess, the daughter of the mountain, he embraced Kesava.
25.82: Thereafter, that goddess, the mother of the worlds, the sharer of half the body of Sankara, the daughter of the mountain Himavan, spoke to Hfslkesa (Krsna).
25.83: "O infinite one, I know the unflinching exclusive devotion you always cherish towards Mahesvara and also towards me, O Kesava.
25.84: You are Narayana, the Supreme Person, the veritable Atman of all. You were born as Devaki's son as you had been entreated to do so by gods formerly.

26.1: See Atman through your own Atman now. There is no difference between us. Sages know us to be identical.
26.2: O Kesava, accept these desired boons from me viz. Omniscience, prosperity and the knowledge pertaining to the Supreme Lord.
26.3: The KP. tries to emphasize the oneness of the trinity of gods in so many places in order to counteract the divisive tendencies in different sects in those times.
26.4: The residents of Kailasa mountain saw that noble- souled Krsna. They worshipped Acyuta in the same manner as the lord of Devas.
26.5: On one occasion, Krsna the increaser of the delight ofDevakI, roamed about in the mountain caves for the purpose of sport.
26.6: On seeing Krsna who was eulogised well, the Gandharva girls as well as the excellent divine Apsaras with brilliant ornaments* (*v.l. with their garments and ornaments slipping down) loved him (passionately).
26.7: Some of them who were skilled musicians were fascinated and overwhelmed with lust, on seeing the handsome son of Devaki and began to sing different songs.
26.8: Some of the girls full of amorous diversion danced in front of him. Some of them looked at him smilingly imbibing the nectar-like beauty of his face.
26.9: Some of the girls took off the excellent ornaments from their limbs and embellished Krsna with due respect— Krsna who himself was an ornament of the worlds.
26.10: Some of them took off the excellent ornaments from his body and bedecked themselves, and adorned Madhava with their own ornaments.
26.11: A certain fawn-eyed damsel, fascinated by passionate love, approached Krsna and kissed his lotus-like face.
26.12: Catching hold of the hand of Govinda, the first cause of the worlds, a certain girl who was deluded by his Maya, took him to her own house.
26.13: Assuming multifarious forms sportively, the lotus-eyed Lord Krsna fulfilled their desires.
26.14: Thus, for a long time, the glorious Hari, Narayana sported in the city of the lord of Devas, fascinating the whole universe with his Maya.
26.15: When a great deal of time elapsed, the residents of Dvaravati became weakened and dispirited as well as frightened on being separated from Govinda.
26.16: Then the powerful Garuda who had been dispatched at the outset, went to the mountain Himavan searching for Krsna everywhere.

27.1: Unable to see Govinda there, he bowed down his head to the sage Upamanyu and came back to Dvaravati again.
27.2: In the meanwhile, thousands of terrible Raksasas came to the splendid city of Dvaraka and threatened it.
27.3: The powerful Garuda whose exploit was similar to that of Krsna killed them in a great battle and saved the splendid city.
27.4: At that time, Narada, the holy sage, who happened to see Kfsna on the peak ofKailasa, went to Dvaravati.
27.5: On seeing the sage Narada, all those residents spoke to him—"Where is the lord and master Narayana Hari?"
27.6: He told them—"Lord Hari, the great Yogin, is sporting about on the peak of Kailasa. I have come here after seeing him."
27.7: O Brahmanas, on hearing his words, Garuda, the most excellent among the fliers (birds), went to the excellent mountain Kailasa through the sky.
27.8: In a mansion embellished with jewels, he sawGovinda the son of Devaki. Lord Hari was seated near the lord of Devas.
27.9: He was surrounded and served by the immortals and the celestial women. The attendants of Mahadeva, Siddhas, and Yogins stood round him.
27.10: Prostrating himself like a staff on the ground and honouring auspicious Sankara, Suparna intimated to Hari what was happening at the city of Dvaraka.
27.11: On seeing Krsna the destroyer of enemies depart¬ ing, the excellent-most Gandharvas (Divine musicians) and Apsaras (celestial ladies) followed that great Yogin, the wielder of conch, discus and mace.
27.12: Hari the Atman of the Universe bade farewell to the ladies. Govinda hastened to the heaven-like splendid city of Dvaravati.
27.13: O leading sages, when the lord, the enemy of the Asuras, went away, the passionately loving women became pale like the night devoid of the moon.
27.14: On hearing about the excellent arrival of Krsna, the citizens immediately decorated the splendid city of Dvaravati.
27.15: The people adorned and embellished the beautiful city with garlands, fastoons, etc., with large banners and by means of flag-staffs both within and without.
27.16: They played on different musical instruments of sweet tone. They blew thousands of conches and broadcast notes of lute all round.
27.17: No sooner did Govinda enter the splendid city of Dvaravati than the women, resplendent in their youthful charms, sang sweet songs.
27.18: Standing on the tops of the mansions, they espied the great lord and began to dance and showered the son of Vasudeva with flowers.
27.19: After entering the city lord Krsna was highly blessed with benedictions. The great Yogin, attended by the gentle ladies, shone in the excellent seat.
27.20: O Brahmanas, in order to pay visit to Krsna the immutable cause of the world, gods, Gandharvas and great elderly sages like Markandeya and others, came there.
27.21: Then Lord Krsna, Hari, got up and bowed down his head to Markandeya who had come there. He offered him his own seat.
27.22: After honouring those sages with his head bent down, Hari, in the company of his followers, bestowed on them what they desired and bade them farewell.
27.23: Then at midday. Lord Hari himself, the lord of Devas, had his ablution, wore white garments and prayed to the sun with palms joined in reverence.
27.24: With his gaze fixed on the sun-god, he duly per¬ formed Japa (repetition) of the holy mantras which are to be muttered. The lord of Devas performed Tarpana for Devas, Pitrsdind sages.
27.25: Entering the temple of the lord in the company of Markandeya, he worshipped the lord of Bhutas (Siva) adorned with Bhasma, (who was) embodied in the Linga.
27.26: On observing all these rites (performed by Krsna) Markandeya, the great sage, laughingly addressed these sweet words to Krsna.
27.27: "Who is the lord propitiated by you by means of these auspicious rites, when you yourself are worthy of being
27.28: You are that Supreme Brahman, the final liberation, the pure one, the highest region (or goal of all). It is for lightening the burden of the earth that you have taken birth in the family of Vrsnis."
27.29: The mighty-armed Krsna, the foremost among the knowers of Brahman, laughingly spoke to him even as all his sons were listening.
27.30: "Undoubtedly everything spoken by you is true. Still, I am worshipping the eternal lord Isana (Siva).
27.31: Undoubtedly there is no obligation on me to do anything. Nor there is anything not obtained by me. Realizing as I do the Supreme Lord Siva, I worship the Lord.
27.32: Those people deluded by Maya do not visualize the lord. I, therefore, worship indicating him to be my original cause.
27.33: There is nothing more meritorious than the worship of Linga in the world. Nothing else is destructive of misfortune. So one should worship Siva embodied in Linga for the benefit of all these people (in the world).
27.34: People expert in the Vedic lore say that what I am, is (God Siva's) symbol (i.e. I am identical with Linga ). I, therefore, worship Lord Siva who is my own pure Atman, by means of my own self.
27.35: There is no doubt that I am his highest form and that I am identical with him. The Vedas declare that undoubtedly there is no difference between both of us at all.'-
27.36: This Lord Mahadeva who is the Supreme Ruler should always be offered sacrifices, worshipped, respected and realized in the Linga form by those who are afraid of the miseries of worldly existence."
27.37: "O excellent god, what is that Linga? Who is being worshipped in the Linga? O Krsna of wide eyes, explain it, as this is an excellent and profound mystery."
27.38: "How did the Linga, the highest region of Isvara, originate formerly to rouse you? O Krsna, it behoves you to explain this now, for the purpose of my enlightenment."
27.39: "O [Lord! Please tell me: Who are you? Whence have you come? Why do you stand here? I am the creator of the worlds. I am the self-born Prapitamaha (the great grand¬ father) of the Universe."
27.40: Thus addressed by Brahma I spoke to him: "I am the creator and the annihilator of worlds again and again."
27.41: When the dispute increased due to the deluding power of Paramesthin (Siva), the great Linga, constituting the nature of Siva, manifested itself before us to enlighten us.

28.1: Then the Unborn lord (i.e. Brahma) said to me— "Let us find out its limits. You go quickly beneath it (to its bottom) and I shall go up."
28.2: Making such an agreement quickly, they (we both) went down and up (of the Linga). But neither the grandsire { of the world Brahma nor I did know the limit (of the Linga). (v.l. even after a hundred years). And they (both of us) came together.
28.3: Thereafter, we were surprised, we got afraid of the Trideni-bearing lord, as we were deluded by his Maya. We began to meditate on the universe and its Lord.
28.4: Uttering Oihkara, the greatest syllable (sound) in a loud tone, and with palms joined in reverence, we eulogised ambhu, the great lord.
28.5: "Obeisance to Sambhu, the physician for the ailment of worldly existence, the root-cause of which is the beginning¬ less Avidya (Maya). Hail to Siva the quiescent Brahman of the form of Lihga.
28.6: Obeisance to one who is stationed in the vast ocean of dissolution and is the cause of dissolution and creation of the universe. Obeisance to Siva, the quiescent Brahman, of the form of Lihga.
28.7: Obeisance to Siva, the quiescent Brahman in the form of Lihga whose symbol is wreaths of flames and is of the form of a column of Are.
28.8: Obeisance to the deity devoid of beginning, middle and end, to one who by nature is spotless refulgence. Obeisance to Siva, the quiescent, infinite Brahman of the form of Lihga.
28.9: Obeisance to the lord of Pradhana and Purusa. Obeisance to the Vedhas (Creator), of the form of the firma¬ ment. Obeisance to Siva, the quiescent Brahman of the form of Lihga.
28.10: Hail to you the immutable, eternal Reality of in¬ comparable splendour, the embodiment of the essence of Vedanta and of the form of Kala (Time or Death).
28.11: Have a look at me, the great Deva; may all your fears be eschewed. Formerly, both of you, the eternal ones, were born of my limbs.
28.12: This Brahma, the grandfather of the worlds is in my right side; Visnu, Hari the protector of the worlds is in the left side, and Kara resides in the heart.
28.13: O my dearly beloved Hari, protect this universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings. O Visnu, I am in the three different forms with the names Brahma, Visnu and Hara.i
28.14: Though I am devoid of Gunas and unsullied, I am threefold due to the attributes for the function of creation, sustenance and dissolution. O Visnu, eschew your delusion and protect this god Brahma, the grand-sire of the worlds.
28.15: It is called Linga, O Brahmana, because it is the Supreme form of the Brahman. O sinless one, thus the glory of Linga has been narrated to you by me.
28.16: Only those who know Yoga, but neither Devas nor Danavas, can understand this. This is the greatest knowledge unrevealed and designated as Siva-lore.
28.17: We pay obeisance to that lord forever whereby those who are endowed with the vision of knowledge see that Lord, subtle and incomprehensible.
28.18: Obeisance to lord Mahadeva, the lord of Devas, to Bhrhgin. Salutations to the blue-throated one, to the mystic secret of the Vedas.
28.19: Hail to the terrible one, to the quiescent Sthanu, to the cause of the Universe, the Brahman, to Vamadeva, to the three-eyed greatest Lord.
28.20: Always pay obeisance to Sankara, Mahesa, Girisa, Siva. Ever meditate on Mahesvara. Ere longyou will be liberat¬ ed from this ocean of worldly existence." Thus the leading sage was advised by Vasudeva.
28.21: This refers to Gautama's curse to Brahmanas who with a desire to return to their hermitages after 12 years' famine were not allowed to do so through persuasion by Gautama. They created a fake cow which died at the prohibitive word of Gautama and thus left him as he was the killer of a cow.
28.22: Aniruddha ofgreat strength was the son of Pradyuma. Both of them were richly endowed with good qualities; they were as if the other two bodies of Krsna himself.
28.23: In the meanwhile, Bhrgu, and other Brahmanas came to Dvaraka in order to see the eternal lord Krsna who had accomplished his mission.
28.24: After bowing to and worshipping them and when they had been comfortably seated alongwith the intelligent Rama, the Atman of the universe (i.e. Krsna) said to them.
28.25: "O great sages, I shall now go to my Supreme abode known as "Visnu's region." All the tasks of my mission have been fulfilled. Be pleased to permit me.
28.26: Now, the inauspicious and terrible Kali Age has set in. In this Age the people will become the followers of sinful activities.
28.27: O excellent Brahmanas, you propagate that perfect knowledge which is beneficial to the ignorant and whereby these will be absolved of the sins of Kali Age.
28.28: Those persons who remember me, the Supreme Lord, even once, in this Kali age, their sins perish.
28.29: Those twice-born ones who worship me everyday with great devotion in the Kali Age, in accordance with the injunction prescribed in the Vedas, will go to my region.
28.30: Thousands of Brahmanas, born of your family, will cherish devotion towards Narayana, in the Kali Age.
28.31: The people who are devoted to Narayana attain the deity that is greater than the greatest. Those who hate Mahes- vara will not attain it.
28.32: The meditation, the Yogic practice, the penance performed, the knowledge obtained, the Yajna and other rites of those people who hate Mahesvara, perish immediately.
28.33: Even he who worships me everyday with single- minded devotion but speaks ill of god Siva, falls into ten thousand hells for ten thousand years.
28.34: Hence, O Brahmanas, the censuring of godofPasupati should be avoided mentally, physically and verbally, by my devotees, by all means.
28.35: Those excellent Brahmanas who had been cursed by Dadhica in the course of the sacrifice performed by Daksa, should be shunned carefully by the devotees in the Kali Age.
28.36: Your descendants on the earth who censure lord I Sana and who have been cursed by Gautama, are not worthy of being conversed with by the excellent Brahmanas."
28.37: All those great sages who were thus addressed by Krsna said Orh (i.e. Amen). Those excellent men hastened to their respective abodes.
28.38: Thereafter, Narayana, Krsna, the pervader of the world, sportingly dissolved his own race and attained that Supreme region.
28.39: Thus the race of kings has been succinctly recoun¬ ted to you. It is impossible to describe it in detail. What is it that you wish to hear further?
28.40: He who reads or listens to the auspicious narration of the races shall be freed from all sins. He is honoured in the heavenly world.
28.41: O Suta, do narrate succinctly to us, the power (v.l. nature) of the four Yugas viz.;—Krta, Treta, Dvapara and Kali.
28.42: The expounder of Brahman was followed and surround¬ ed by his disciples and their disciples. Then Arjuna eschewed his grief and prostrated himself on the ground like a staff.
28.43: Sitting on the banks of the river and surrounded by his disciples, the sage, the great Yogin Krsnadvaipayana said to him.

29.1: O lord of men, I shall tell you the Tugadharmas succi¬ nctly, as it is not possible to explain them in detail by me.
29.2: O Partha, the first Yuga is said to be Krta by scholars, then comes Treta-, the third Yuga is Dvapara and Kali is the fourth.
29.3: It is said that meditation and penance are enjoined (as the important dharma) in the Krta Age, attainment of perfect knowledge in the Treta Age, performance of sacrifices in the Dvapara Age and charitable gifts in the Kali Age.
29.4: Brahma is the deity in the Krta Yuga, in Treta, it is lord Ravi (sun), the deity in Dvapara is Visnu and Mahesvara is the lord in Kali Age.
29.5: Brahma, Visnu and the sun-god, all these are wor¬ shipped in the Kali Age too. But the Pinaka-bearing lord Rudra is worshipped in all the four Yugas.
29.6: In the first Krtayuga, Dharma is glorified as having full four feet. In Treta it becomes three-footed while it is two-footed in Dvapara.
29.7: O scorcher of enemies, the people stayed on moun¬ tains and in the ocean (or on the seashore). They had no fixed abode. O Brahmanas, in due course of time, in the Yuga called Treta, their taste and pleasure disappeared.
29.8: All of them were delighted and contented and free from ailments, thanks to that Siddhi. Again after the lapse of some more time, they were overcome by their greed.
29.9: Being afflicted by mutually opposite types of climates, they made coverings (shelters) and clothes. After devising means that counteracted the contradictory climatic changes, they began to think of agriculture and trade.
29.10: When the Kalpa trees were lost alongwith honey in the Treta Yuga, further Siddhis appeared before them.
29.11: Due to the inevitability of the course of events and as it was the effect of Treta Yuga, people forcibly occupied the river banks and fields as well as mountains.
29.12: They seized trees, hedges and medicinal herbs forcibly. Due to this misdemeanour and aberration of theirs, the medicinal herbs entered Earth.
29.13: Later, king Prthu milked these out of Earth at the behest of Pitamaha, god Brahma, grabbed them all in their senseless fury against each other.
29.14: In the beginning of all Dvapara Yugas, they (i.e. the Vedas )are divided into four by Vedavyasas. (They are many because they are different in the different sets of four Yugas). The Vedas differ due to the difference (or delusion) in the visions among the sons of sages or altered visions.
29.15: The Saihhitas of RK, Yajus and Saman are being recited by the great sages by introducing Mantras and Brahmanas with due changes in accents and syllables.
29.16: After reflection and investigation they become free from attachment. Then, they begin to see defects. It is due to realisation of defects that knowledge becomes possible in Dvapara.
29.17: O Brahmanas, the behaviour in Dvapara is due to mixture of Rajas and Tamos. The Dharma that prevailed in the first (i.e. Krta) Yuga continued in Treta Age.
29.18: It becomes agitated in Dvapara Yuga and it is destroyed in Kali Age.
29.19: VV. 54-55 constitute an explanatory paraphrase of dhata yathapirvam akalpayat /
29.20: Epidemics of fatal disease, perpetual fear of hunger and starvation, fear of droughts and destruction of countries prevail in Kali Age.
29.21: Utterly bad subjects born in Kali Yuga are im¬ pious, deficient in food and highly furious but lacking in brilli¬ ance, liars and greedy.
29.22: The fear of subjects is heightened due to ill per¬ formance of Yajnas, faulty study of the Vedas, evil conducts and misleading heretical scriptures and defects in the rites of Brahmanas.
29.23: In this age, twice-born persons do not study the Vedas or perform sacrifices (or worship). People of low intellec¬ tual capacity will perform sacrifices and study the Vedas.
29.24: In Kaliyuga, the Sudras will have close association with the Brahmanas by the use of spells and incantations as well as through the sharing of beds, seats and food.
29.25: The kings who will be mostly Sudras will harass the Brahmanas. Killing of the foetus and heroes will be of common practice among kings.
29.26: The twice-born people will not perform ablutions. Harms, Japas, offer of charitable gifts, worship of deities and other holy rites.
29.27: In Kali age, the people censure Mahadeva, Purusottama, Brahmanas, Vedas, Dharmasastras and Puranas.
29.28: People perform various rites not found in the Vedas. The Bralunanas would not have any interest in their prescribed pious rites and duties.
29.29: People will have evil activities and conduct of life. They will be surrounded by useless dissembling heretics. They will be begging one another on many occasions.
29.30: In Kali age, common people will begin to sell cooked food. The Vedas will be sold on the cross-roads, and youthful maidens will sell their bodies.
29.31: When the close of Yuga is imminent, Sudras calling themselves Jims (subduers of sense organs) will perform holy rites by shaving off their heads, wearing ochre robes and black-antelope skins and keeping their teeth white.
29.32: People will be plunderers of crops of others and- deprivers of (other people's) clothes. Thieves will be robbers
29.33: It is stated in Smrtis that in the Kali age there will be prevalence of extreme misery, shortness of life-span, •exhaustion of physical bodies, spread of sickness, sinful activi¬ ties arising from attachment to Adharma.
29.34: There will be some people wearing ochre-coloured robes, some going naked (Jainas), some bearing skulls (Kapali- kas), some will sell Vedas while others will sell sacred places.
29.35: Seeing the Brahmanas seated, people of petty intellect will make them move; Sudras depending upon kings may even strike the leading Brahmanas.
29.36: O tormentor of enemies, Sudras will be occupying lofty seats in the middle of Brahmanas. In Kali age, as a result of the influence of times, the king will dishonour the Brahmins.
29.37: Brahmanas, of insufficient learning, possessing ill-luck and no great strength will begin to serve Sudras with flowers, ornaments and other auspicious articles.
29.38: O king, Sudras will not cast a glance at the Brahmanas, worthy of respect and worship. It is the Brahmanas who would stand at their threshold awaiting an opportunity for service.
29.39: In Kaliyuga, the Brahmanas, dependent on the Sudras, hover round and serve the Sudras seated in their vehicles and eulogise them by songs of praise and prayer.
29.40: Dependent on Sudras, they teach them Vedas. Due to the calamity of appeasing those without Vedas, they resort to terrible atheism.
29.41: Even the excellent ones among Brahmanas will sell the merit of penance, sacrifices and arts. As to Sannyasins, there will be hundreds and thousands.
29.42: O ruler of men, destroying their own pious rites, they •do not attain that region. They sing about deities with worldly songs.
29.43: In Kali age, there will be Brahmanas as well as
29.44: When perfect knowledge and the holy rites are lost, when the whole world has become inactive, insects, mice, and serpents will harass human beings.
29.45: Those Brahmanas who had been burnt completely in the fire of the curse of goddess Sati formerly during Daksa's sacrifice, will be reborn in the families of Brahmanas.
29.46: In the Kaliyuga, towards the close of that age, they, with their mind overwhelmed by Tamas, will censure Mahadeva. Theirs will be a futile pursuit of Dharma.
29.47: Although the Kali age is defective in many respects, there is one great good point in it viz. a man derives very great merit without any great strain.
29.48: Hence, after reaching the Yuga belonging to Mches- vara, a Brahmana shall, by all means and with special care, seek refuge in Rudra, I Sana.
29.49: Those who bow down to Isana of three eyes and wearing the elephant's hide, shall become delighted in their minds and attain to Rudra and his greatest region.
29.50: Just as the obeisance paid to Rudra certainly yields all desired fmits, one shall not derive that benefit by making salutations to other deities.
29.51: In the Kali Yuga of such a nature, the only means of purifying defects is the obeisance rendered to Mahadeva, meditating on him and offering charitable gifts—So says the Sruti.
29.52: Hence, if one wishes to attain the highest beatitude one should eschew all gods other than god Siva and resort to the three-eyed Mahesvara.
29.53: Futile indeed is the very life, the charitable gifts, the penance and the performance of sacrifice of those people who do not worship Rudra, Siva, who is saluted by Devas.
29.54: Obeisance to Rudra the great God of gods, Mahadeva, to the trident-bearing Tryambaka, Trinetra (the three-eyed god). Salutations to the preceptor of Yogins.
29.55: Hail to the lord of Devas, to Mahadeva, to Vedhas (creator), to Sambhu. Obeisance forever to Sthanu, to Siva the Paramesthin.
29.56: Salutations to Rudra accompaniedjby Uma, to Maha- grasa (devouring all in a mouthful), the cause of the universe. I resort to the three-eyed celibate worthy of being a refuge.
29.57: I bow to the extremely red god, who puts forth his tongue, to the sungod, Paramesthin, the fierce Pasupati, to the terrible deity, to the refulgent sun, to the Supreme penance (v.l. beyond darkness).

30.2: In the Manvantaras, both past and the future, all people are of identical names and forms and they identify themselves with the same.''
30.3: Thus advised by the holy sage, Svetavahana (Arjuna) •cherished in himself the greatest and unswerving devotion to Isana.
30.4: He made obeisance to the holy sage Krsnadvaipayana who was omniscient, the creator of all, who was established as Visnu himself.
30.5: Stroking Partha, the conqueror of enemies' cities who bowed to him, by means of his splendid hands, sage Vyasa spoke to him again.
30.6: "You are blessed, favourite with the Lord. In all the three worlds there is certainly no other person like you who is a devotee of Sankara, and the conqueror of enemies' cities.
30.7: You have directly perceived that lord Rudra who has tiniversal vision, has faces all round, who is the very embodi¬ ment of the imiverse.
30.8: That divine lordly knowledge has been precisely understood by you. The eternal Hrsikesa (Vyasa, his incarna¬ tion) himself has recounted it to you, out of delight.
30.9: Do you go to your own abode. It does not behove you to grieve over it. With the greatest devotion seek refuge in 5iva worthy of being the refuge."

31.1: O holy sage, it behoves you, the omniscient one, to dispel one of our doubts. There is nothing which is unknown to you, the great sage,
31.2: On hearing the words of Jaimini, Sage Krsnadvai- payana bowed down to the bull-bannered deity (Siva) and said in a majestic tone.
31.3: O excessively blessed one, excellent, very nice. O sage, I shall explain what has been asked by you. It is the secret of secrets. May the other sages too hear it.
31.4: This eternal perfect knowledge was explained by Isvara formerly. It is a great secret disliked by non-intelligent persons but resorted to by men of subtle vision.
31.5: This excellent knowledge, the best among all types of knowledge, should not be imparted to one who has no faith, nor to one who is not a devotee of Paramesthin; nor should it be given to one who is not the knower of Vedas.
31.6: The goddess, seated on her divine seat on the peak of Aleru asked Mahadeva, Isana, the enemy of the Tripuras.
31.7: O Mahadeva, O lord of Devas, O destroyer of the distress of devotees, how can a man perceive you, the lord, in a short while?
31.8: O Sankara, the systems of Sarhkhya and Yoga, the penance, the meditation, the Vedic path of action and other things as well, they say, are very strenuous and tedious.
31.9: This knowledge, excluded by (i.e. incomprehensible to) the ignorant, is of great mysterious meaning and is not to be revealed to anybody else. I shall explain it to you, precisely, as mentioned by great sages.
31.10: The city of Varanasi is my secret-most holy centre. It is the cause that enables all living beings to cross the ocean of worldly existence.
31.11: The great-souled devotees of mine who have taken to the observance of my vows and who adhere to those great observances, stay at that place.
31.12: It is the most excellent of all holy centres; the best of all abodes; the most excellent of all types of knowledge; it is my sacred place Avimukta.
31.13: The holy centres and shrines situated in other places, in heaven, on earth and in cremation grounds are all found here.
31.14: My abode is not in contact with the earth, it is in the firmament. Those who are not liberated do not perceive it; the liberated ones observe it through the mind.
31.15: This city is known as Avimukta (not deserted by me). It is the well-known cremation ground. O beautiful women; it is here that I annihilate this universe after becoming Kala.
31.16: O goddess, of all my secret abodes, this is the most lovable to me. Whenever my devotees go here, they enter me alone.
31.17: What is offered there as a charitable gift, the Japa performed there, the Homas, the Yajhas and the penances performed there, the meditation, the study of the Vedas and the knowledge pursued there—all these shall be inexhaustible in benefit here.
31.18: All sins accumulated previously in the course of thousands of births are annihilated, the moment one enters the holy centre of Avimukta.
31.19: A sinner dying in Avimukta never goes to hell. All of them blessed by Isvara, attain the great goal.
31.20: Realising that salvation is very difficult to achieve and the world is very terrible, a man should strike his feet with stone and stay on in Varanasi.
31.21: O Paramesvarl, it is very rare that a living being attains penance * there, but to him who dies there, the goal is conducive to liberation from worldly existence.
31.22: O daughter of the lord of mountains, thanks to my grace, sin perishes here. But insensible men, deluded by my Maya do not perceive it.
31.23: Those who are deluded and enveloped by darkness do not perceive Avimukta. They enter in the midst of faeces, urine and semen again and again.
31.24: If buffeted by hundreds of calamities, a person enters and stays at my city, he attains the highest beatitude from which there is no return.
31.25: He enters the abode of Siva that is free from births, deaths and old age. That is the goal of those who seek salvation, who have no further fear of death.
31.26: Avitnukta is the greatest knowledge, Avimukta is the greatest region, Avimukta is the greatest principle, Avimukta is the greatest and the most auspicious Bliss.
31.27: At the end I bestow the greatest knowledge and the greatest region, on those who take an irrevocable vow of staying in Avimukta.
31.28: Therefore, one shall not commit sins physically, mentally or verbally. O excellent Brahmanas, this is the secret of the Vedas and the Puranas.
31.29: After saying this, the holy lord Vyasa, the most excellent among the knowers of the Vedas, went to Varanasi along with his excellent disciples.
31.30: For derivation see the legend in VV. 16-18. For its glory cf. NP. II. 49.6-10, Pd. P. I. 34.10. In fact KP. VV. 3-29 in this chapter are practically the same as Pd. P. I. 34.1-25.
31.31: After worshipping Mahadeva, there, alongwith his disciples, the great sage recounted its greatness to the sages whose souls are purified by meditation.
31.32: This is that stainless Linga Othkara by name. It is very splendid. By its sheer memory, one is released from all sins.
31.33: It is here that the excellent supreme knowledge of five Ayatanas (five-faced Siva?), capable of granting absolute emancipation from Saihsara, has been always worshipped by the sages.
31.34: Here the glorious Lord Rudra, god Mahadeva himself who has assumed five-bodied {Pancayatand) form and who bes¬ tows Moksa on living beings, sports.
31.35: What is mentioned as the knowledge pertaining to Pasupati and which has five topics or imports is this stainless Linga situated at Oihkara.
31.36: The five topics are super-quiescence, supreme peace, knowledge, stability and cessation. These five are the five aspects of the Linga of Isvara.
31.37: The Linga designated as Oihkara is called Pancaya- tana (having five abodes) as it is the support of the five deities viz. Brahma and others.
31.38: If at the time of death, one remembers the Linga pertaining to Isvara, the unchanging Pancayatana Linga, one enters the Supreme light and bliss.

32.1: O prominent Brahmanas, on the bank of Matsyodari, there is an excellent place, the secretmost, auspicious spot of the extent of a Gocarma known as the excellent Oihkara.
32.2: After saying this, the great sage, Krsna, the son of Parasara, went to see the Krttivasesvara Linga of the Trident¬ bearing Lord.
32.3: After worshipping it along with his disciples, the holy sage, the most excellent among the knowers of Brahman, men¬ tioned the greatness of Krttivasas (the deity wearing elephant hide) to the Brahmanas.
32.4: "Formerly aDaitya assumed the form of an elephant in this place and came near Bhava (Siva) to kill those Brahmanas who worship the lord here everyday.
32.5: O Excellent Brahmanas, in order to protect those devotees, the three-eyed Mahadeva, favourably disposed to the devotees, appeared out of the Lihga.
32.6: Contemptuously Kara killed the Daitya of the form of an elephant with his trident. Its hide he made his robe. Hence the lord is Krtti vases vara.
32.7: O leading sages, the sages attained the greatest Siddhi here. They attained the greatest region with their own body.
32.8: Those who are glorified as Vidya, Vidyesvaras, Rudras and Sivas surround the Krttivasesvara Linga forever, and abide here.
32.9: There is no doubt about this that those persons who realize that this Kaliyuga is terrible and full of evil do not leave Krttivasa and achieve their highest object in life.
32.10: In other places, salvation may or may not be attained in the course of a thousand births. But at the shrine of Krt- tiva, salvation is obtained in the course of a single birth.
32.11: They say that this abode is the place of residence of all Siddhas. It is protected by MahMeva, Sambhu, the lord of Devas.
32.12: In every Yuga, the Brahmanas of self-control, the masters of the Vedas, worship Mahadeva. They perform the japa of the Satarudriya Mantra.
32.13: Meditating in their hearts on Sthanu, Siva, who is present within everyone, they forever eulogize the three-eyed Mahadeva.
32.14: Siddhas verily sang songs to those Brahmanas who have resided in Varanasi and seek refuge in Krttivasa.
32.15: After securing the birth in the families of the Brah¬ manas very rare in the world and liked by all the worlds, the ascetics have recourse to meditation, perform the Japa of Rudra and meditate on Mahesa in their minds.
32.16: The leading sages in Varanasi propitiate the lord and the Ruler. Without attachment and desire, they perform Yajnas, eulogise Rudra and bow down to Sambhu.
32.17: Obeisance to Bhava of pure emotions and splendour; I resort to Sthanu, Girisa, the ancient deity. I remember Rudra who has entered my heart. I know that Mahadeva of many forms."
32.18: The legend explaining the name Piidca-mocana (deliverer from the joni of Pisacas or goblins) is given below in VV. 15-35. The legend is repeated in Pd. P.I. 34.
32.19: O Brahmanas, he took his bath in the holy centre Picamocana, performed the Tarpana rite for the Pitrs in accordance with the injunctions and worshipped Sulin (the trident-bearing deity).
32.20: Those sages saw a wonderful event there in the company of their preceptor, whereby they accepted the great¬ ness of the shrine and bowed down to Hara, Girisa.
32.21: A certain tiger of hideous features approached the excellent Kapardisvara shrine in order to devour a hind.
32.22: The hind was much frightened in her mind. In her agitation,' she ran round and round the shrine and ultimately submitted to the tiger.
32.23: The tiger of very great strength tore the hind with its sharp claws and on seeing the leading sages, it went away to another isolated forest.
32.24: When that hind fell dead in front of Kapardisvara a great flame of fire lustrous like the sun was seen in the sky.

33.2: The firmament-dwellers showered flowers on his head. He became the Ganesvara himself and vanished at the same instant.
33.3: On seeing this wonderful event, (the disciples) the -chief of whom was Jaimini asked the infallible preceptor about the greatness of Kapardisvara.
33.4: After bowing down to the bull-bannered deity and sitting in front of the lord, the holy sage recounted the greatness ■of Kapardisa.
33.5: This excellent Lihga of Lord Kapardisvara should be worshipped assiduously and with care and eulogised by the Vedic hymns.
33.6: To the Yogins of quiescent minds, who regularly meditate here, the accomplishment of Yogic Siddhi occurs ■within six months. There is no doubt about it.
33.7: If one takes one's bath in the holy tankofPisa- camocana near this place and worships this lord, the sins like Brahmana-slaughter and other similar sins perish.
33.8: O Brahmanas, formerly a great ascetic of praiseworthy holy rites, well-known as Sahkukarna, worshipped the trident¬ bearing lord.
33.9: He performed the Japa of the Pramva (Orh) having' the form of Rudra. He ■worshipped Rudra constantly by means of flowers, incense etc. and hymns, obeisances and circumambula- tions,
33.10: Taking up a perpetual initiation and celibacy the Yogic soul stayed there. Once he saw a very hungry ghost who had arrived there.
33.11: He was a mere skeleton of bones covered with bare skin and was heaving deep sighs again and again. On seeing him, the leading sage was overwhelmed with great sympathy.
33.12: He said—"who are you, sir? From which land have you come over to this place?" The ghost who was being afflicted by hunger spoke these words to him.
33.13: "I was a Brahmana in my previous birth. I was endowed with plenty of wealth and foodgrains. I was blessed with sons, grandsons, etc. I was eager to maintain the family.
33.14: Neither Devas, nor cows nor guests were worshipped by me. Even a minor meritorious deed, even the slightest of good action was not performed by me.
33.15: Once Lord Rudra, with the lordly bull for his vehicle, the lord of the universe was seen at Varanasi. He was touched and bowed to by me.
33.16: Then, ere long, I passed away. O sage but the terrible face of Yama was not seen.
33.17: Having fallen into this ghoulish form of existence, I am so much afflicted by hunger and so much overwhelmed with thirst that I do not know what is beneficial or detrimental to me.
33.18: O holy lord, if you see any remedy for uplifting me from this ghostly type of existence please do it. I bow down to you. I seek refuge in you."
33.19: Sahkukarna who was addressed thus, said to the ghost:—"There is none else in this world like you, who is of the greatest meritorious deeds.
33.20: Since, formerly. Lord Siva, the Lord of the universe, was seen, touched and saluted by you, who else can be equal to you in this world?
33.21: That Piiaca (ghost) who had been thus advised by the merciful sage, remembered the three-eyed excellent lord Kapardlsvara, the ruler of the universe, concentrated his mind and took his ablution into the holy pond.
33.22: As a result of the plunge, he died in the vicinity of the sage. He was then seen in an aerial chariot that resembled the sun himself,bedecked with divine ornaments with his beauti¬ ful crest marked by the moon.
33.23: Rising up and surrounded by Rudras stationed in heaven and by incomprehensible Yogins, he shone like the rising sun, the lord of all, surrounded by Valakhilya sages and others.
33.24: In heaven, Siddhas and Devas began to eulogise; the charming celestial Apsaras danced; the Gandharvas, Vidyadharas, Kinnaras and others showered flowers with bees hovering round them.*
33.25: After attaining spiritual enlightenment through the grace of divine Lord, he, being eulogised by groups of eminent sages, entered the foremost sphere of the sun consisting of three Vedas where Rudra himself shines.
33.26: On seeing the goblin-like ghost liberated, the sage was delighted. He mentally thought of Mahesa, Rudra, the foremost of the wise. He bowed down to and eulogised Kapardin.

34.1: I seek refuge in you, the Brahman, (i.e. Vedas), the golden one, abiding in the hearts of Yogins, devoid of beginning. I seek refuge in you stationed in heaven, the holy great sage, composed of Brahman.
34.2: I bow unto you, beyond Brahman, Sambhu endowed with a thousand feet, eyes and heads, having a thousand arms,
34.3: For ever I bow down to and seek refuge in Siva, Lord Isa, the other shore of Brahman, from whom the universe origi¬ nates and by whom the auspicious one, the universe is dissolved and all these have been brought up.
34.4: I bov/ down to you, the Sole Rudra, beyond all ■symbols, of unmanifest form, self-luminous, the Lord of con¬ sciousness, the Supreme Lord who is beyond Brahman and beyond whom nothing exists.
34.5: I bow unto your form which is beyond Brahman {Brahmapara), the lord whom the Yogins visualize after attaining Samadhi (the trance) wherein the Sabija form is eschewed (i.e. in the nirvikalpa samadhi) when the Yogins become one with the Supreme Atman.
34.6: I bow forever to you who are the ultimate form of BTzhmdin {Brahma-para) which transcends names and which has no special gratifications and whose form is beyond the ken of sight.
34.7: I pay obeisance for ever to that ultimate shore of Brahman whom those who are absorbed in Vedic discussion realise to be formless, the very embodiment of knowl¬ edge about Brahman, undifferentiated, one without a second yet they perceive it in multifarious form.
34.8: I bow for ever to your huge form called Kala from which the Pradhana and Ancient Purusa have come out as a Vivaria (illusion), to whom Devas pay respects, which is en¬ veloped in brilliance.
34.9: Forever, I seek refuge in Mahesa, I resort to Sthanu, Girisa, the ancient deity. I resort to Siva, the moon-crested Hara, the wielder of the Pinaka bo'w."
34.10: After eulogising Lord Kapardin thus, Sankukarna fell on the ground like a staff, repeating the auspicious Pranava Mantra ( Orti).
34.11: At the same instant the greatest Linga of the nature •of Siva manifested itself there; it was of the nature of knowledge
34.12: That pure spotless sage Sahkukarna, of the nature of the soul of all, became merged in the stainless Linga; It was something miraculous.
34.13: This great secret, the greatness of Kapardin has been narrated. Due to Tamas Guna no one understands it, even a scholar becomes deluded in this regard.
34.14: The devotee who listens to this sin-destroying episode will be absolved of all sins and shall attain forever the proximity to Rudra.
34.15: The pure-hearted person who always reads the great hymn called Brahmapara both in the morning and at midday shall attain Yoga.

34.18: Beholding intently (at the river), the holy sage Dvai- payana whose mind was purified with deep devotional feelings and who was himself the knower of the rites of ablutions, took his holy bath along with sages.
34.19: After duly performing Tarpana rites to Devas, to the sages, to the PUrs, he performed the worship of trident-bearing Madhyamesvara, I Sana god Siva.
34.20: Then the tranquil devotees of Pasupati who had besmeared their bodies with Bhasma (sacred ashes) came to see Madhyamesvara, Isvara, Rudra.
34.21: On seeing sage Dvaipayana surrounded by his disciples, the Brahmanas worshipped him suitably and spoke these words.
34.22: "Who are you, O great sage? Whence have you come along with your disciples?" Paila and other disciples spoke to those sages purified by means of piety.
34.23: "This is the son of Satyavati, the holy sage Krsna- dvaipayana. He is Vyasa and Hrsikesa (Visnu) himself by whom the Vedas have been classified."
34.24: To him, god Mahadeva, the Pinaka-bearing lord himself, became the son named Suka, with a portion of his part.
34.25: He has resorted to Mahadeva, Sankara, with heart and soul and the greatest devotion and has attained that perfect divine knowledge."
34.26: Thereafter, all those devotees of Pasupati, with hairs standing on end due to excessive delight, spoke to Vya, the son of Satyavati, with a quiescent mind.
34.27: "O holy lord, the knowledge of Paramesthin has been acquired by you by the grace of the lord of Devas. It is the greatest knowledge pertaining to Mahesvara.
34.28: Hence, expound this excellent, unrevealed mystic secret to us without any agitation. May we see the lord quickly after hearing about him through your oral utterance."
34.29: After dismissing those disciples the chief of whom was sage Sumantu, the most excellent among the knowers of Yoga explained to the Yogins that great knowledge.
34.30: At that same instant a pure and excellent mass of brilliant light manifested itself there. Those Brahmanas got themselves merged there and vanished in a moment.
34.31: Thereafter, the revered sage, the most excellent one among the knowers of Brahman, recalled Paila and all other disciples and recounted the greatness of Madhyamesa.
34.32: It is here that the supreme lord Siva indulges in sport alongwith his consort Parvati, in the company of ganas.
34.33: It is here that formerly Krsna, son of DevakI, Hrsikesa stayed continuously for one year, surrounded by Pasupatas.

35.1: Many of his disciples devoted to the vow of celibacy attained perfect knowledge, through his advice and perceived Mahesvara.
35.2: Lord Mahadeva, the blue-red complexioned God appeared directly before Krsna. The bestower of boons that he is, the lord conferred upon him excellent boons.
35.3: "O embodiment of the Universe! Those of my devo¬ tees who worship Govinda with due rites and formalities, will have engendered in them this divine knowledge pertaining to Isvara (Siva).
35.4: There is no doubt in this that you will be the Isa, worthy of being worshipped and meditated by the twice-born people devoted to me, thanks to my grace."
35.5: The sins due to Brahmana-slaughter, etc. of those people who visit the lord of Devas and who meditate on Pinaka- bearing lord, perish quickly.
35.6: Those of Brahmanas who, though engaged in sinful activities, give up their life (at this sacred place) will attain to that Supreme abode. No doubt need be entertained in this respect.
35.7: O Brahmanas! They are verily the blessed ones who take a holy dip in MandakinI and worship the great God, the excellent Madhyamesvara (Lihga).
35.8: O Brahmanas, anyone of these rites, viz. ablution, charitable gifts, penance, Sraddha and offering of the balls of rice (as pinda) performed duly at this place sanctifies upto the seventh generation.
35.9: If they are performed at Kuruksetra when the sun is devoured by Rahu (at the time of solar eclipse), the benefit that a man derives therefrom is tenfold."
35.10: After saying thus, the great Yogin stayed fora long time in the vicinity of Madhyamesa, worshipping Mahesvara.

36.1: O excellent Brahmanas, on one occasion while he stayed there, Vyasa, of unmeasured splendour wandered for the sake of alms but he did not get anything.
36.2: Then the sage was overwhelmed by great anger. He said "I shall create obstacles for all men staying here whereby their achievement will become deficient."
36.3: At the very same instant, the great goddess, the sharer of half the body of Sankara, assumed human form and appeared there out of affection.
36.4: Then the great goddess told him again—"O sage, since you are irascible, you must not stay here as you are always ungrateful."
36.5: Thus addressed, the holy lord realised the great goddess Siva through meditation. With humility he bowed down, eulogised her with excellent hymns and said:
36.7: O Sankari, be pleased to permit me to enter the city on the Astami and Caturdasi (eighth and the fourteenth) day." saying 'so be it', the goddess permitted him and disappeared.
36.8: Thus the holy sage Vyasa, the ancient great Yogi realised the good points of the holy centre, and stayed near it.
36.9: It is after knowing that Vyasa was stationed in the holy centre, that the learned men resorted to it. Hence a man should by all means, reside in Varanasi.
36.10: He who reads the greatness of Avimukta, listens to it or narrates it to the quiescent Brahmanas, attains the Supreme goal.

38.1: O highly blessed king, listen. O scion of the family of Bharata, what you ask me shall be explained. Visiting Prayaga is excellent as it is destructive of the sins of men."
38.2: O ruler of men, lord Mahadeva, Rudra, stayed there. Lord Brahma, the self-born deity, abides there alongwith other Devas.
38.3: "O holy lord, I wish to hear about the fruit of pilgrimage to Prayaga. What is the goal attained by the persons who die there? What is the merit that accrues to those who take their ablutions there?
38.4: Mention the benefit derived by those who reside in Prayaga. Indeed this is known to you. Please relate it to me. Obeisance be to you."
38.5: "O dear one, I shall recount to you the fruit of ablutions in Prayaga. It was heard by me as it was being recount¬ ed by great sages formerly.
38.6: This is the holy place sacred to Prajapati. It is well- known in the three worlds. By taking their bath here, people attain heaven. Those who die here are not reborn.
38.7: Brahma and other Devas gathering together at that place afford protection. There are many other holy places there, that dispel sins.
38.8: I cannot recount it in even hundreds of years. I shall succinctly narrate to you the glory of Prayaga.
38.9: Prayaga extends over an area of sixty thousand Dhanus—that includes Gahga. The sun-god with seven horses to his chariots always protects Yamuna.
38.10: Indra himself abides in Prayaga. Hari protects this zone which is revered by all Devas.
38.11: Mahesvara, armed with the trident, protects the Myagrodha (holy fig tree) for ever. Devas protect the holy place that is auspicious and dispels all sins.
38.12: By touching or being sprinkled with its water, a person is honoured in the region of gods, even if such a man be sickly, indigent or infuriated.
38.13: It is the redeemer of Pitrs and destructive of sins. The ocean of worldly existence is crossed by those who take up residence at Prayaga.
38.14: Leading sages say that one derives desired pleasures if one casts off one's life with special efforts after reaching the confluence ofGahga and Yamuna.
38.15: Hence, one should not receive gifts in Tirthas or holy shrines. A Brahmana should be alert in the case ofall conditions.
38.16: W. 26-27 Cf. Mt. P. 106. 34-42; Pd. P. 1.43.34-42; NP. 11.63. 140-149. The textual similarity is worth noting.
38.20: He who resorts to the root of the holy Banyan tree and abandons his life there, goes to the northern Kurus and rejoices for endless time.
38.21: O tiger among kings, Prayaga is well-known in the three worlds. The middle of Gahga and Yamuna is known as the 'loin-region' of the Earth.®
38.22: A person of praiseworthy religious vows, who per¬ forms ablutions in the confluence attains the benefit equal to that of performing the Rajasuya and the horse-sacrifice.
38.23: O dear one, neither at the instance of the mother nor at the report of the common people should your mind to perform pilgrimage to Prayaga, be dissuaded.
38.24: O scion of the family of Kurus, sixty thousand Tirthas and other sixty crores of sacred places are present here (at Prayaga).
38.25: The goal attained by one who gives up his life at the confluence of Gahga and Yamuna is the same as obtained by a learned man who has renounced the world as a Sannyasin and who is endowed with Yogic power.

38.27: Thus on seeing the holy place Prayaga, the greatest region, one is absolved of all sins like the moon from the clutches of Rahu.

39.8: As long as the bones of a man lie in Gahga, he is honoured in the heavenly world for so many thousand years.®
39.9: Gahga is the sacred-most of the sacred places. It is the holiest of holy rivers. It is the bestower of salvation for all living beings, even to the great sinners.
39.10: Gahga is easy of access everywhere but is of difficult access in three places viz. at Gahgadvara (place of source), at Prayaga and at its confluence with the ocean.*
39.11: There is no goal (means of salvation) on a par with Gahga to the living beings whose minds are overwhelmed by sins and who are in search of way of deliverance from sins.

41.1: From him was born Prthu, whose son was Nakta; Nakta's son is known as Gaya; Nara was Gaya's son; his son was Viraj.
41.2: The chapter deals with ancient Indian astronomy which according to modern advances in that science is outdated—especially the distances and positions and dimensions of planets mentioned appear to be rather imaginary. The credit of creating the world is given to the sun and god Mahadeva is- identified with him (v. 27).
41.3: The following are the worlds originating from the- Cosmic Egg viz. Bhurloka, Bhuvarloka, Svarloka, Maharloka, Janaloka, Tapoloka, and Satyaloka.
41.4: O leading Brahmanas, the extent of space illuminated by the rays of the sun and the moon is called Bhurloka in the Puranas.
41.5: Bhuvarloka is of the same extent in area and circum¬ ference as the Bhurloka and is above it upto the sphere of the sun.
41.6: The sphere of the moon is stationed at a distance of a hundred thousand Yojanas from the sphere of the sun. The entire stellar sphere shines at a distance of a hundred thousand Yojanas above the moon.
41.7: O Brahmanas, Budha (the Mercury) is at a distance of two hundred thousand Yojanas from the stellar sphere. Usanas (the Venus) is stationed at the same distance from the Mercury.
41.8: Ahgaraka (the Mars) is stationed at the same dis¬ tance from Sukra (the Venus). The preceptor of Devas, Brhaspati (i.e. the Jupiter) is stationed at a distance of two hundred thousand Yojanas fromBhauma (i.e. the Mars).
41.9: Sauri (i.e. the Saturn) is stationed at a distance of two hundred thousand Yojanas from the Jupiter. The sphere of the seven sages (i.e. the Great Bear) shines at a distance of a hundred thousand Yojanas from the sphere of the planets.
41.10: Above the sphere of the seven sages, at a distance of a hundred Yojanas is stationed Dhruva (the Pole star) * Dhruva is verily the pivot or the axis of the stellar system. Lord Visnu, Narayana, Dharma himself is abiding there.
41.11: The diameter of the sun's sphere is known as nine thousand Yojanas. The circumference is three times that.
41.12: The extent of the moon is known as twice the extent of the sun. Svarbhanu (i.e. the evil planet Rahu) assumes a size equal to them and approaches them.
41.13: He is created with a.spherical shape after extracting the shadow of the earth. The extensive third abode of Rahu is full of darkness.
41.14: Sukra (the Venus) is one-sixteenth of the dimension of the moon in extent. Brhaspati (the Jupiter) should be known as one-fourth less than the dimension of the Venus.
41.15: Both Bhauma (the Mars) and Saura (the Saturn) are known as being a one-fourth less than Brhaspati (the Jupiter). In extent and circumference, Budha (the Mercury) is one-fourth less than the above two.
41.16: The forms of the stars and the constellations taken together in a body are equal to Budha in extent as well as in circumference.
41.17: The stars and constellations are smaller or larger in mutual comparison by five hundred, four hundred, three hundred or two hundred Yojanas (in extent).
41.18: The stellar spheres are lesser in extent (nikrstani). * Their dimensions are only half a Yo\zxa,{Tojananyardha-rnatrani*). None (no heavenly body) is smaller than they.
41.19: The three planets stationed above traverse the greatest distance. The planets Saturn, Jupiter and Mars should be known as moving slowly.
41.20: Four great planets are beneath them: the Sun, the moon, the Mercury and the Venus have fast movements.
41.21: When the sun moves in Daksinayana (southern transit) it traverses far below the previous planets.
41.22: Enlarging its sphere the moon traverses above it. The entire stellar sphere moves above the moon.
41.23: Budha (the Mercury) is above the star, the Venus is above the Mercury, Vakra (the Mars) is above the Venus and the Jupiter is above the Mars.
41.24: The Saturn is above that (the Jupiter) and further above is the sphere of the seven Sages (Great Bear). Dhruva (Pole star) is stationed above the seven sages.
41.25: O excellent Brahmanas, the chariot of the sun is nine thousand Yojanas long. The length of the shafts is twice that.
41.26: Its axle is one crore and a half and seven million {niyuta) Yojanas and the wheel is fixed there.
41.27: The entire Kalacakra (wheel of time) is fixed there in the form of the year having three times seven (v.l. three) Nabhis (i.e. naives), five spokes and six rims.
41.28: ** O excellent Brahmanas, the second axle of the
41.29: The length of both the axles is half that of both the yokes. The short axle with the short pole of the chariot has the Polar star as its support.
41.30: The second axle to which the wheel of the chariot is fixed is on the Manasa mountain. His seven horses are the seven metres. Understand their names.
41.31: The horses of the sun are the metres viz. Gayatri (It has 6 syllables in a quarter); Brhati (9 syllables in a quarter or foot); Usnik (7 syllables in a foot); Jagati (12 syllables in a foot), Pankti (10 syllables in a foot); Anustup (8 syllables in a foot) and Tristup (11 syllables in a foot).

42.1: Taking with him the constellations of the Zodiac, Pitamaha (i.e. the sun-god), the lord of gods, moves rapidly to the Southern direction like a discharged shaft.
42.2: O leading Brahmantis! In the seven continents, the sun at mid-day and at middle of the night always stands face to face (i.e. faces opposite directions).
42.3: The rising and the setting of the sun are always opposed (to each other comparatively) in different directions as well as in the intermediate quarters, O prominent Brahmanas.
42.4: While this Lord (the sun-god) moves like the rotating wheel of a potter, he makes the night* as he leaves the earth, O Brahmanas.
42.5: The three worlds are illuminated by the rays of the sun; that has been declared £is Trailokya (a triple world) by good persons, to the people, O Brahmanas.
42.6: There is no doubt in this that the three worlds have their original source in the Aditya (the sun god). The entire universe including Devas, Asuras and human beings originates from it.
42.7: The lustrous sun conquered the worlds of Rudra, Indra, Upendra (Visnu), Candra (the moon), of the leading Brahmanas and the heaven dwellers. ♦He conquered the worlds.
42.8: This sun is the Atman of all; is the lord of the worlds; he is the great Deva and Prajapati; he is the root of this world; he is the greatest deity.
42.9: There are other twelve Adityas (sons of Aditi); they are Devas who are authorised and who fulfil their duties. They are the parts of Visnu; they are the different forms of Visnu.
42.10: All including Gandharvas, Yaksas, serpents, Kinnaras and others make obeisance to the thousand armed deity; the leading sages worship the ancient deity the embodi¬ ment of the Chandas (vedic metre) and the eternal Brahman, by means of different Yajnas.
42.11: These twelve Adityas (Sun-gods) are supposed to be the portions or amSas of the sun-god and the twelve forms of Visnu. The provision of ages, Gandharvas, celestial damsels, etc. to each (minor) sun-god is a Puranic concept of solar paraphernalia. The deities of these attendants (Gandharvas, Apsaras, Yaksas, sages, etc.) are detailed in this chapter.
42.12: The Gandharvas and Apsaras worship him by singing songs and performing dances. The presiding deities of villages — (Gramanis), Yaksas and Bhutas hold the reins.
42.13: The serpents bear the lord of Devas; the Yatudhanas go ahead of him. The Valakhilyas (thumb-sized sages) surround the rising sun and go along with him till sunset.
42.14: They are glorified as those who give heat, shower rain, shine, blow, create, and annihilate the inauspicious activities of living beings.
42.15: These followers of the sun accompany the sun as he moves on in heaven. They are always seated in the aerial chariot that has the velocity of wind and that can go wherever it wishes to go.
42.16: They protect all living beings in due order of Yugas (v.l. end of Yugas) by showering rains, giving heat and by delighting the people.
42.17: Lord sun gives heat in accordance with the virility, penance, yogic power and the inherent vigour of Devas.
42.18: That Prajapati (Lord of subjects) is the cause of demarcation of night and day. The sun nourishes perpetually the Pitrs, Devas, human beings and others.
42.19: The great lord, the radiant sun, is Lord Mahesvara himself. The eternal blue-necked lord (Siva) of those who know the Vedas, shines forth.
42.20: It is this god who is the progenitor of the world, Paramesthin. The knowers of the Vedas, the embodiments of the Vedas know that his abode is in the Sun-god Aditya.
42.21: Puranas evince great interest in cosmogony, cosmology and cosmo¬ graphy as an area lying between philosophy and theology. They are more interested in trying to solve the mysteries of the supreme soul and the universe rather than the matter-of-fact world around them. This topic has been discussed practically in all Puranas like the Bh.P. (V. 16.1-25), NP. (1.3.37-49). Though the imaginary nature of their concepts is obvious, we may, however, suggest that the idea of the planets receiving their power and existence from the rays of the sun might be the Puranic way of suggesting that all planets are born from the sun.
42.22: O Brahmanas, out of his rays which are the illuminators of the worlds, the most excellent among them are the seven rays, the purifiers of the houses (v.l. graha-yonayah —"sources of planets").

43.1: This Susumla is described to be moving sideways (horizontally) and upwards. The ray that is said to be Harikesa is the nourisher of the lustre of the stars.
43.2: The ray Visvakarman perpetually nurtures Budha (the Mercury). The ray that is named Visvasravas always nourishes Sukra (the Venus).
43.3: The ray which is well-known as Sarhyadvasu, develops the Mars. The lordly ray Arvavasu affords nourishment to the Jupiter very well.
43.4: He has a thousand rays exuding chillness, rain and heat. Among them four hundred Nadis (i.e. rays) of the variegated forms shower rains.
43.5: The rays called Candragas, Gahas, Kancanas, Satanas* which are called Nectarine {Amrta) create showers.
43.6: The sun deposits Amrta (nectar) in the immortal beings. Thus in the three beings he deposits the three articles. O Brahmanas, there are eight other planets which are presided over by the sun.
43.7: They are: the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, Rahu and Ketu.
43.8: The planets are fixed to the Pole star {Dhruva) by the wind-rays whirling in their own orbit, they follow the sun.
43.9: They move about like the firebrand in a circle, when urged by the whirlwind. Since the wind propels and bears them, it is named Pravaha.
43.10: In the bright half of the month, when the sun is in the opposite direction of the moon, the other (back) side of the moon is always filled up with those brilliant rays. (v.l. ever according to the order of the days.)
43.11: (In the dark half) when the moon is emaciated and drunk by Devas, the sun nourishes it forever, O Brahmanas, by a single ray called Susumla.
43.12: This body of the moon is developed by the prowess of the sun. By gradually becoming bigger everyday, it is seen complete and full on the Full Moon day.
43.13: O Brahmanas, the deities drink the full moon consist¬ ing of Amrta in the course of half a month. This is so because their diet consists of Nectar.
43.14: When a fifteenth of it remains, consisting of a single digit, the groups of Pitrs drink the last portion in the afternoon.
43.15: They drink for the period of two Lavas, * the Kala of the moon that remains. The digit of the moon is constituted of nectar and is auspicious.
43.16: By imbibing the nectar called Svadha oozing out of the rays on the new Moon day, the Pitrs become satisfied for the period of a month.
43.17: O excellent one, the moon is not destroyed but only the nectar is drunk to the fill. Thus the decrease and increase of the moon are dependent on the sun.
43.18: The chariot of the son of the moon (i.e. Budha—the Mercury) is yoked to eight horses that have the velocity of the wind and that are born of water. He moves about all round in that chariot.
43.19: The chariot of Sukra (the Venus) is yoked to ten horses bom of the Earth. The beautiful golden chariot of Bhauma (the Mars) is yoked to eight horses.
43.20: All these blessed ones are fixed to Dhruva by the strings of wind. The planets, stars, constellations and other abodes are entirely fixed to Dhruva. They whirl and cause others to whirl by the wind-made reins.
43.21: Maharloka is above the Pole Star. It extends to a crore of Yojanas. O leading Brahmanas, the persons inhabiting there are entitled to the life span of a Kalpa.
43.22: Janaloka is above Maharloka. Its spatial magnitude is two crores of Yojanas. Sanaka and other sons of Brahma are stationed there.
43.23: Tapoloka is above Janaloka. It extends to three crores of Yojanas. Devas called Virajas who live there are immune from consumption by fire.
43.24: Satyaloka is above the world of Prajapatis. It extends to six crores of Yojanas. It is a region where there is no death again. It is also named as Brahmaloka.
43.25: Here in the Satyaloka god Brahma, the preceptor of the world, the soul and the efficient cause of the Universe ever abides in the company of Yogis by drinking the Supreme nectar of Yoga.
43.26: Quiescent recluses, the perpetual Brahmacarins (celi¬ bates), Yogins, Siddhas, ascetics and performers of the Japa of Paramesthin reside there.
43.27: His (Brahma's) city which is very difficult to attain resembles one crore of suns in brilliance and is emblazoned with clusters of fiery flames and as such it is impossible for me to describe it.
43.28: There in the city of Brahma is the abode of Narayana also. The glorious Hari, the wielder ofMaya lies down there.
43.29: It is called Visnuloka. There is no return from there to Sarhsara. The noble-souled people who have resorted to Janardana can go there.
